## So, here are 18 actors that wrote their own roles, and nailed them, obviously!

## 1.[Matt Damon](https://www.buzzfeed.com/noradominick/winter-movie-preview-2026) and [Ben Affleck](https://www.buzzfeed.com/spenceralthouse/famous-actors-who-are-really-tall) – [_Good Will Hunting_](https://www.buzzfeed.com/kristenharris1/famous-movie-lines-improvised)

![Image 3](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/7/19/asset/9c75313c37a2/sub-buzz-2067-1670442566-9.jpg?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

 Miramax 

Even though they'd had minor forrays into acting, neither had gotten the opportunity to show what they could do, and this was part of the [reasoning](https://faroutmagazine.co.uk/why-ben-affleck-matt-damon-wrote-good-will-hunting/) for writing what turned out to be their big break, _Good Will Hunting._

Speaking about the intention behind writing the movie, Ben said this: "The whole thing of _Good Will Hunting_ was really just to make – at the time – a video cassette that was like an acting reel. Like, we can’t get the job to show that we can do interesting stuff, so the whole thing was to have a reel and show casting directors, and so we’ll write these parts for ourselves."

The two had to keep things as cheap as possible, hence the movie mainly being "talking in rooms." It clearly paid off big time, as their "acting reel" ended up winning an Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay alongside [Robin Williams](https://www.buzzfeed.com/ravenishak/90s-disney-film-quiz)' award for Best Supporting Actor.

## 2.[Gene Wilder](https://www.buzzfeed.com/crystalro/willy-wonka-chocolate-factory-kids-now) – _Young Frankenstien_

![Image 5](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/10/asset/797651446f6b/sub-buzz-2262-1670496852-100.jpg?downsize=600:*&output-format=auto&output-quality=auto)

 20th Century Fox 

Considered one of the greatest comedies of all time, Gene Wilder is more commonly known for his [starring](https://inews.co.uk/culture/film/young-frankenstein-first-scene-gene-wilder-mel-brooks-93877) role in _Young Frankenstein._ It was actually Gene – not director Mel Brooks – who had the idea for the movie. Gene thought of the movie in 1972 and wrote down four pages of a screenplay. Eventually, Mel Brooks would get involved, with his experience helped bring Gene's character _to life_.

Funny enough, those four pages of the screenplay that Gene wrote down actually made it into the final edit! The movie is now a frequent part of "best comedy movies of all time" [lists](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/best-comedy-movies-funniest-films-time/15young-frankenstein-1974/), and evidently, there was no one better to portray the brainchild of Gene than Gene himself!

## 3.Sylvester Stalone – _Rocky_

![Image 7](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/11/asset/3b4b0119da8f/sub-buzz-494-1670499297-74.png)

 United Artists 

The way that _Rocky_ got made is a [remarkable](https://www.forbes.com/sites/tomward/2017/08/29/the-amazing-story-of-the-making-of-rocky/?sh=254f091f560b) story. Sylvester was broke, living in California, trying and failing to find work. Then, one night, he went to see Muhammad Ali fight Chuck Wepner and the idea for _Rocky_ just came to him.

Within three days he had his script finished (only about a third of it would be used in the final film), and he showed it to the producers at a casting call that he didn't get the part for. The producers offered him$360,000 for the script on the condition that someone other than Sylvester would play Rocky because they wanted a Hollywood name. But he knew that if the film was a success, he would never forgive himself for not being the star.

So, Sylvester held out, insisting that he'd only let them make the film if he could play Rocky, and they eventually relented, giving him a $1m budget to make and star in the film. _Rocky_ went on to be nominated for nine Academy Awards (winning three), and become one of the most profitable film franchises of all time!

## 4.Donald Glover – _Atlanta_

![Image 11](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/12/asset/87d8f2597ad5/sub-buzz-4550-1670501845-19.jpg)

 FX 

When Donald Glover decided to leave _Community_ after season five, it was to focus on more personal projects including the writing and producing of _Atlanta,_ which he also starred in.

There was a variety of motivations for creating the show, Donald [said](https://www.polygon.com/tv/2016/8/9/12415520/donald-glover-community-atlanta-childish-gambino) that "what was important to me was that this show was personal and that this show had a specific take." Describing the series, Donald said: "The show is about being Black and it's hard to write that down."

_Atlanta_ ran for four seasons and won a host of awards including a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series for Glover himself.

## 5.Bill Hader – _Barry_

![Image 15](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/13/asset/afbf0a41090d/sub-buzz-458-1670506054-91.jpg)

 HBO 

Bill's motivation for writing[Barry](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2022/apr/25/bill-hader-hitman-comedy-barry-disease-keeps-us-making-bad-choices)was definitely more about the narrative than his starring role. In fact, he finds it difficult to write for himself, saying. "I'm not that great at writing big characters for myself and I tend to get excited about the other characters."

His passion for the show and disregard for his own characters means that he's actually forgotten to write Barry into an episode – he then received a note from HBO saying he had to be in the episode.

Having said before that he could never direct himself because he couldn't bare to look at his face, he chose to put that aside when he was inspired to write _Barry_ after visiting the set of _Better Call Saul._ The dark, violent humour that _Barry_ is full of indeed has a _Better Call Saul_ quality, and the series has been a great success, as highlighted by its three Emmys!

## 6.Billy Bob Thornton – _Sling Blade_

![Image 19](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/13/asset/fd62039a6065/sub-buzz-506-1670507454-64.jpg)

 Miramax Films 

Billy's initial [vision](https://www.creativescreenwriting.com/im-pretty-anti-violence-i-dont-want-to-do-more-movies-about-violence-billy-bob-thornton/)for the main character, Karl, in _Sling Blade_ came when he was working on a cable movie and was pretty down about his prospects, saying "I saw all the 'real' actors around me, people who had a real job — I was basically an extra with a couple of lines—I just felt depressed." He remembers coming up with the character while looking into a mirror:

"I went into the trailer at lunchtime and started looking at myself in the mirror, making faces at myself. [...] I don’t know what I said. And then I did that opening monologue, all at once, and I didn’t know where it came from. It was kind of spooky."

While the film isn't autobiographical, a lot of the characters in the movie are based on people Billy knew, and the stories are inspired by things that happened where he was brought up. Billy started performing it as a one-man show, but with help from his agent, he was able to make it into a movie that he wrote, directed, and starred in. The movie won the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, adapted from the show, and Billy was also nominated for Best Actor in a Leading Role.

## 7.Nia Vardalos – _My Big Fat Greek Wedding_

![Image 23](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/14/asset/dc127d601e6b/sub-buzz-519-1670508555-71.png)

 IFC Films 

Nia's inspiration for the movie was her own [experiences](https://metro.co.uk/2022/04/20/nia-vardalos-reveals-that-my-big-fat-greek-wedding-almost-never-happened-16501118/) growing up in a large but close Greek family. Despite gaining somewhat of a cult following, the movie was initially rejected, as Nia shared on Twitter:

"When agents and managers said my script wasn’t good and actors shouldn’t write, I recall wondering why they were angry. They fired me. So, I changed the material into a solo stage show. Rita Wilson saw the play and said, 'This should be a movie'”

Thankfully Rita Wilson decided to help make it happen, and Nia herself starred as the lead in a movie that many would find inspiring due to its honest storytelling and personality. She stressed the importance of never giving up, saying: "You can’t make anyone embrace change, marginalised voices or new ideas. So love yourself. And write your story."

## 8.Emma Thompson – _Sense and Sensibility_

In the mid-nineties, Emma Thompson was well aware of the dearth of interesting roles for women in Hollywood and decided to take things into her own hands. Using those hands she wrote the screenplay for Jane Austin's _Sense and Sensibility_, a movie with a host of punchy female roles. On starring in the movie herself, she [said](https://ew.com/article/1995/12/15/emma-thompson-write-part/) ”I wrote [a role]... and then I bloody well played it.”

Emma would become the first person to win an Oscar for acting AND screenplay writing when she took home the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay for _Sense and Sensibility,_ having won Best Actress a few years previously.

Emma would go on to write various other screenplays, some of which she'd star in too, including _Nanny McPhee_ and _Bridget Jones's Baby._

## 15.Phoebe Waller-Bridge – _Fleabag_

![Image 55](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/17/asset/cfdcdac250b4/sub-buzz-878-1670520337-17.jpg)

 BBC 1 

Phoebe, who didn't actually base _Fleabag_ on herself, wrote the play when she was in a state of flux. Speaking about how the character came about she [said](https://www.elle.com/uk/life-and-culture/culture/a28445306/phoebe-waller-bridge/) this:

"When I was feeling at my most down and angry and rageful standing at the precipice of whatever that is in your mind and I looked at the bottom of the chasm and the very bottom was _Fleabag_. So I was like 'I'm going to write her to stop me from becoming her.'"

The one-woman show was written and performed by Pheobe at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, where it won the famous Fringe First Award. That really kickstarted things for Pheobe, who went on to star in the TV adaptation of _Fleabag_ that would make her an international sensation.

Her stardom has only risen since then of course, with her going on to be a writer on _Killing Eve_ and being one of the writers for _No Time To Die._

## 16.Rob Delaney and Sharon Horgan – _Catastrophe_

![Image 59](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/17/asset/811c935653e7/sub-buzz-877-1670521425-17.jpg)

 Channel 4 

When the pair decided to write a show, each had the same goal – to make something that they could relate to, and something that they actually _wanted_ to make. Talking about this, Sharon said: "We wanted to make a brutally honest relationship comedy, and use comedy to talk about tricky things."

Rob was on the same page, saying that the industry is so tough, so if you're going to try to do something, you may as well go for exactly what you want: "It’s so hard to get a show made. You might as well talk about exactly what you want to talk about."

The two drew from their own personal experiences with pregnancy, parenthood, and their different backgrounds to create a comedy show that would also deal with serious issues without the rose-tinted glasses, as Rob put it: "A show that purports to be about real life but doesn’t have those things to me wouldn’t be a real show."

The show was a great success, running for four seasons!

## A lot of actors are super talanted, and when they decide to write their own movie or TV show, they rightly think "you know who would be good for this role? Me!"

[Video 1](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/18/asset/ab4ec3b86f05/anigif_sub-buzz-670-1670524140-69.gif?output-format=mp4)

## So, here are 18 actors that wrote their own roles, and nailed them, obviously!

## 1.[Matt Damon](https://www.buzzfeed.com/noradominick/winter-movie-preview-2026) and [Ben Affleck](https://www.buzzfeed.com/spenceralthouse/famous-actors-who-are-really-tall) – [_Good Will Hunting_](https://www.buzzfeed.com/kristenharris1/famous-movie-lines-improvised)

![Image 3](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/7/19/asset/9c75313c37a2/sub-buzz-2067-1670442566-9.jpg?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

 Miramax 

Even though they'd had minor forrays into acting, neither had gotten the opportunity to show what they could do, and this was part of the [reasoning](https://faroutmagazine.co.uk/why-ben-affleck-matt-damon-wrote-good-will-hunting/) for writing what turned out to be their big break, _Good Will Hunting._

Speaking about the intention behind writing the movie, Ben said this: "The whole thing of _Good Will Hunting_ was really just to make – at the time – a video cassette that was like an acting reel. Like, we can’t get the job to show that we can do interesting stuff, so the whole thing was to have a reel and show casting directors, and so we’ll write these parts for ourselves."

The two had to keep things as cheap as possible, hence the movie mainly being "talking in rooms." It clearly paid off big time, as their "acting reel" ended up winning an Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay alongside [Robin Williams](https://www.buzzfeed.com/ravenishak/90s-disney-film-quiz)' award for Best Supporting Actor.

## 3.Sylvester Stalone – _Rocky_

![Image 7](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/11/asset/3b4b0119da8f/sub-buzz-494-1670499297-74.png)

 United Artists 

The way that _Rocky_ got made is a [remarkable](https://www.forbes.com/sites/tomward/2017/08/29/the-amazing-story-of-the-making-of-rocky/?sh=254f091f560b) story. Sylvester was broke, living in California, trying and failing to find work. Then, one night, he went to see Muhammad Ali fight Chuck Wepner and the idea for _Rocky_ just came to him.

Within three days he had his script finished (only about a third of it would be used in the final film), and he showed it to the producers at a casting call that he didn't get the part for. The producers offered him$360,000 for the script on the condition that someone other than Sylvester would play Rocky because they wanted a Hollywood name. But he knew that if the film was a success, he would never forgive himself for not being the star.

So, Sylvester held out, insisting that he'd only let them make the film if he could play Rocky, and they eventually relented, giving him a $1m budget to make and star in the film. _Rocky_ went on to be nominated for nine Academy Awards (winning three), and become one of the most profitable film franchises of all time!

## 6.Billy Bob Thornton – _Sling Blade_

![Image 19](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/13/asset/fd62039a6065/sub-buzz-506-1670507454-64.jpg)

 Miramax Films 

Billy's initial [vision](https://www.creativescreenwriting.com/im-pretty-anti-violence-i-dont-want-to-do-more-movies-about-violence-billy-bob-thornton/)for the main character, Karl, in _Sling Blade_ came when he was working on a cable movie and was pretty down about his prospects, saying "I saw all the 'real' actors around me, people who had a real job — I was basically an extra with a couple of lines—I just felt depressed." He remembers coming up with the character while looking into a mirror:

"I went into the trailer at lunchtime and started looking at myself in the mirror, making faces at myself. [...] I don’t know what I said. And then I did that opening monologue, all at once, and I didn’t know where it came from. It was kind of spooky."

While the film isn't autobiographical, a lot of the characters in the movie are based on people Billy knew, and the stories are inspired by things that happened where he was brought up. Billy started performing it as a one-man show, but with help from his agent, he was able to make it into a movie that he wrote, directed, and starred in. The movie won the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, adapted from the show, and Billy was also nominated for Best Actor in a Leading Role.

In the mid-nineties, Emma Thompson was well aware of the dearth of interesting roles for women in Hollywood and decided to take things into her own hands. ## 16.Rob Delaney and Sharon Horgan – _Catastrophe_

![Image 59](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2022-12/8/17/asset/811c935653e7/sub-buzz-877-1670521425-17.jpg)

 Channel 4 

When the pair decided to write a show, each had the same goal – to make something that they could relate to, and something that they actually _wanted_ to make. Talking about this, Sharon said: "We wanted to make a brutally honest relationship comedy, and use comedy to talk about tricky things."

Rob was on the same page, saying that the industry is so tough, so if you're going to try to do something, you may as well go for exactly what you want: "It’s so hard to get a show made. You might as well talk about exactly what you want to talk about."

The two drew from their own personal experiences with pregnancy, parenthood, and their different backgrounds to create a comedy show that would also deal with serious issues without the rose-tinted glasses, as Rob put it: "A show that purports to be about real life but doesn’t have those things to me wouldn’t be a real show."

The show was a great success, running for four seasons!

*   Creative control: writing gives actors influence over story, tone, and character arc. 
*   Collaboration with directors/producers: scripts often evolve jointly, with actors contributing rewrites or improvisational passages.

Notable examples (actor credited as writer or co-writer)

*   Charlie Chaplin — The Gold Rush (1925), City Lights (1931), Modern Times (1936), The Kid (1921): wrote, directed, starred; seminal examples of actor-as-author in early cinema. 
*   Orson Welles — Citizen Kane (1941) and others: co-wrote, directed, and starred; foundational case of multi-role auteur. 
*   Woody Allen — Annie Hall (1977), Manhattan (1979), many others: routinely wrote and starred in his films. 
*   Billy Wilder — While primarily a writer-director, Wilder occasionally appeared in small roles and frequently collaborated with actors who contributed; example mostly shows writer-actor overlap in classic Hollywood circles. 
*   Sylvester Stallone — Rocky (1976): wrote the screenplay and starred as Rocky Balboa; script was pivotal to his career launch. 
*   Matt Damon & Ben Affleck — Good Will Hunting (1997): co-wrote the screenplay together and starred (Damon co-starred), winning the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay. 
*   Greta Gerwig — Lady Bird (2017), Little Women (2019): wrote and directed and did cameo/voice roles; demonstrates actor-writer-director crossover in modern indie/mainstream film. 
*   Kenneth Branagh — Henry V (1989), Much Ado About Nothing (1993): adapted/rewrote and starred; frequent actor-writer-director. 
*   Lena Dunham — Tiny Furniture (2010), Girls (TV): wrote, directed, and starred in projects that launched careers. 
*   Emma Thompson — Sense and Sensibility (1995): adapted Austen’s novel and acted in the film; earned an Oscar for screenwriting. 
*   Ben Stiller — Zoolander (2001), Tropic Thunder (2008, co-writer/producer): often co-writes projects he stars in. 
*   Greta Scacchi / smaller independent examples: many actor-driven indies where lead performers write or co-write scripts to realize personal projects. 

Common variations

*   Sole writer and star: actor is credited as the primary screenwriter and plays the lead (e.g., Stallone in Rocky; Chaplin in many silent-era films). 
*   Co-writer and star: actor shares screenplay credit with collaborators (e.g., Damon/Affleck on Good Will Hunting; Stiller on multiple comedies). 
*   Uncredited rewrites or improvisation: actors often rewrite dialogue on set or improvise scenes; these contributions sometimes go uncredited but materially shape the final film (common with comedy teams and actor-directors). 
*   Actor-writer-director-producer: full creative control across roles (Welles, Chaplin, Woody Allen on many films, Kenneth Branagh on Shakespeare adaptations).

Patterns by industry and era

*   Silent/early sound era: actor-writers like Chaplin were common because filmmaking was small-scale and auteur-driven. 
*   Studio era: fewer actors wrote entire screenplays, but some (or their agents) pushed for story input. 
*   New Hollywood and indie era onward: more actors write to create vehicles, especially when traditional roles are scarce. Contemporary streaming and indie production ecology further increase opportunities for actors to originate scripts.

How to verify authorship on a specific film

*   Check screen credits (on-screen, IMDb, BFI, AFI). 
*   Look for Writers Guild of America (WGA) credit listings or copyright registrations for official authorship. 
*   Production histories and biographies often document actor contributions, rewrites, and uncredited work.

Short list of especially influential cases to start with

*   Charlie Chaplin — City Lights, Modern Times 
*   Orson Welles — Citizen Kane 
*   Woody Allen — Annie Hall, Manhattan 
*   Sylvester Stallone — Rocky 
*   Matt Damon & Ben Affleck — Good Will Hunting 
*   Emma Thompson — Sense and Sensibility

Conclusion  
Actors have long written their own scripts, ranging from early auteurs who single-handedly wrote, directed, and starred, to contemporary actors who co-write or contribute extensive on-set rewrites. The practice is common enough across film history that many celebrated movies began as projects authored by their leading actors.

Yes — many films have been written (fully or in part) by the actors who star in them. Examples span studio pictures, independents, comedies, and auteur-driven projects. Below is a concise, structured survey illustrating common patterns and notable cases.

Why actors write

*   Desire for a tailored role: actors write to create parts that suit their strengths or break typecasting. 
*   Creative control: writing gives actors influence over story, tone, and character arc. 
*   Collaboration with directors/producers: scripts often evolve jointly, with actors contributing rewrites or improvisational passages.

Notable examples (actor credited as writer or co-writer)

*   Charlie Chaplin — The Gold Rush (1925), City Lights (1931), Modern Times (1936), The Kid (1921): wrote, directed, starred; seminal examples of actor-as-author in early cinema. 
*   Orson Welles — Citizen Kane (1941) and others: co-wrote, directed, and starred; foundational case of multi-role auteur. 
*   Woody Allen — Annie Hall (1977), Manhattan (1979), many others: routinely wrote and starred in his films. 
*   Billy Wilder — While primarily a writer-director, Wilder occasionally appeared in small roles and frequently collaborated with actors who contributed; example mostly shows writer-actor overlap in classic Hollywood circles. 
*   Sylvester Stallone — Rocky (1976): wrote the screenplay and starred as Rocky Balboa; script was pivotal to his career launch. 
*   Matt Damon & Ben Affleck — Good Will Hunting (1997): co-wrote the screenplay together and starred (Damon co-starred), winning the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay. 
*   Greta Gerwig — Lady Bird (2017), Little Women (2019): wrote and directed and did cameo/voice roles; demonstrates actor-writer-director crossover in modern indie/mainstream film. 
*   Kenneth Branagh — Henry V (1989), Much Ado About Nothing (1993): adapted/rewrote and starred; frequent actor-writer-director. 
*   Lena Dunham — Tiny Furniture (2010), Girls (TV): wrote, directed, and starred in projects that launched careers. 
*   Emma Thompson — Sense and Sensibility (1995): adapted Austen’s novel and acted in the film; earned an Oscar for screenwriting. 
*   Ben Stiller — Zoolander (2001), Tropic Thunder (2008, co-writer/producer): often co-writes projects he stars in. 
*   Greta Scacchi / smaller independent examples: many actor-driven indies where lead performers write or co-write scripts to realize personal projects. 

Common variations

*   Sole writer and star: actor is credited as the primary screenwriter and plays the lead (e.g., Stallone in Rocky; Chaplin in many silent-era films). 
*   Co-writer and star: actor shares screenplay credit with collaborators (e.g., Damon/Affleck on Good Will Hunting; Stiller on multiple comedies). 
*   Uncredited rewrites or improvisation: actors often rewrite dialogue on set or improvise scenes; these contributions sometimes go uncredited but materially shape the final film (common with comedy teams and actor-directors). 
*   Actor-writer-director-producer: full creative control across roles (Welles, Chaplin, Woody Allen on many films, Kenneth Branagh on Shakespeare adaptations).

Patterns by industry and era

*   Silent/early sound era: actor-writers like Chaplin were common because filmmaking was small-scale and auteur-driven. 
*   Studio era: fewer actors wrote entire screenplays, but some (or their agents) pushed for story input. 
*   New Hollywood and indie era onward: more actors write to create vehicles, especially when traditional roles are scarce. Contemporary streaming and indie production ecology further increase opportunities for actors to originate scripts.

How to verify authorship on a specific film

*   Check screen credits (on-screen, IMDb, BFI, AFI). 
*   Look for Writers Guild of America (WGA) credit listings or copyright registrations for official authorship. 
*   Production histories and biographies often document actor contributions, rewrites, and uncredited work.

Short list of especially influential cases to start with

*   Charlie Chaplin — City Lights, Modern Times 
*   Orson Welles — Citizen Kane 
*   Woody Allen — Annie Hall, Manhattan 
*   Sylvester Stallone — Rocky 
*   Matt Damon & Ben Affleck — Good Will Hunting 
*   Emma Thompson — Sense and Sensibility

Conclusion  
Actors have long written their own scripts, ranging from early auteurs who single-handedly wrote, directed, and starred, to contemporary actors who co-write or contribute extensive on-set rewrites. The practice is common enough across film history that many celebrated movies began as projects authored by their leading actors.

Ethan Green Hawke was born on November 6, 1970 in Austin, Texas, to Leslie Carole (Green), a charity worker, and James Steven Hawke, an insurance actuary. His parents were students at the University of Texas at the time but divorced when Ethan was 5 years old. His mother raised him alone for the next five years, moving around the country, until she remarried in 1981 and the family settled in Princeton Junction, New Jersey.  
  
He attended West Windsor-Plainsboro High School and then transferred to the Hun School of Princeton and it was while he was there that he began taking acting classes at the McCarter Theatre on the Princeton campus. His early ambition had been to be a writer, but as a result of the acting lessons and appearances in student productions he persuaded his mother to allow him to attend an audition for a role in a sci-fi adolescent adventure, [Explorers (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0089114/?ls). He got the role (along with [River Phoenix](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000203/?ls)) but although the movie was favourably reviewed, it met with little commercial success which discouraged Hawke from pursuing further movie roles for several years.  
  
He was admitted to the prestigious Carnegie-Mellon University to study theatre but his studies were interrupted when he won his break-through role opposite [Robin Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000245/?ls) in [Dead Poets Society (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097165/?ls) and he did not complete his degree. He then appeared in numerous films before taking a role in the Generation X drama [Reality Bites (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110950/?ls) for which he received critical praise. He starred in the romantic drama [Before Sunrise (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112471/?ls), and its later sequels [Before Sunset (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0381681/?ls) and [Before Midnight (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2209418/?ls).  
  
His subsequent acting career was a mix of theatre work (earning a number of awards and nominations, including a Tony Award nomination for his role in "The Coast of Utopia" at the Lincoln Center in New York), and a mix of serious and more commercial movies, notably [Gattaca (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119177/?ls) (where he met his first wife, [Uma Thurman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000235/?ls)) and [Training Day (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0139654/?ls).  #### [5. George Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000123/?ref_=ls_t_5)

[The Ides of March (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1124035/?ref_=ls_knf_5)

George Timothy Clooney was born on May 6, 1961, in Lexington, Kentucky, to [Nina Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm6460343/?ls) (née Nina Bruce Warren), a beauty pageant queen, and [Nick Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0167040/?ls), a former anchorman and television host (who was also the brother of singer [Rosemary Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0167041/?ls)). He has Irish, English, and German ancestry. Clooney spent most of his youth in Ohio and Kentucky, and graduated from Augusta High School. He was very active in sports such as basketball and baseball, and tried out for the Cincinnati Reds, but was not offered a contract.  
  
After his cousin, [Miguel Ferrer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001208/?ls), got him a small role in a feature film, Clooney began to pursue acting. His first major role was on the sitcom [E/R (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086704/?ls) as Ace. More roles soon followed, including George Burnett, the handsome handyman on [The Facts of Life (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078610/?ls); Booker Brooks, a supervisor on [Roseanne (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094540/?ls); and Detective James Falconer on [Sisters (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101199/?ls). Clooney had his breakthrough when he was cast as Dr. Doug Ross on the award-winning drama series [ER (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108757/?ls), opposite [Anthony Edwards](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000381/?ls), [Noah Wyle](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001864/?ls) and [Julianna Margulies](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000523/?ls).  
  
While filming "ER" (1994), Clooney starred in a number of high profile film roles, such as [Robert Rodriguez](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001675/?ls)'s [From Dusk Till Dawn (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0116367/?ls), and [One Fine Day (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117247/?ls), opposite [Michelle Pfeiffer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000201/?ls). In 1997, Clooney took on the role of Batman in [Joel Schumacher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001708/?ls)'s [Batman & Robin (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118688/?ls). The film was a moderate success in the box office, but was slammed by critics, notably for the nipple-laden Batsuit. Clooney went on to star in [Steven Soderbergh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001752/?ls)'s [Out of Sight (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120780/?ls), [Terrence Malick](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000517/?ls)'s [The Thin Red Line (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120863/?ls), and [David O. Russell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0751102/?ls)'s [Three Kings (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120188/?ls).  
  
In 1999, Clooney left "ER" (1994) (though he would return for the season finale) and appeared in a number of films, including [O Brother, Where Art Thou? (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0190590/?ls), [The Perfect Storm (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0177971/?ls) and [Ocean's Eleven (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0240772/?ls). Collaborating once again with [Steven Soderbergh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001752/?ls), Ocean's Eleven (2001) received critical acclaim, earned more than $450 million at the box office, and spawned two sequels: [Ocean's Twelve (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0349903/?ls) and [Ocean's Thirteen (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0496806/?ls).  
  
In 2002, Clooney made his directorial debut with [Confessions of a Dangerous Mind (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0270288/?ls), an adaptation of TV producer [Chuck Barris](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0057567/?ls)' autobiography. This was the first film under the banner of Section Eight Productions, a production company he founded with [Steven Soderbergh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001752/?ls). The company also produced many acclaimed films, including [Far from Heaven (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0297884/?ls), [Syriana (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0365737/?ls), [A Scanner Darkly (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405296/?ls) and [Good Night, and Good Luck. (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0433383/?ls). Clooney won his first Oscar for Best Supporting Actor in Syriana (2005), and was nominated for Best Director and Best Original Screenplay for Good Night, and Good Luck. (2005).  
  
In 2006, Section Eight Productions was shut down so that Soderbergh could concentrate on directing, and Clooney founded a new production company, Smokehouse Productions, with his friend and longtime business partner, [Grant Heslov](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0381416/?ls).  
  
Clooney went on to produce and star in [Michael Clayton (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0465538/?ls) (which earned him an Oscar nomination for Best Actor), directed and starred in [Leatherheads (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0379865/?ls), and took leading roles in [Burn After Reading (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0887883/?ls), [The Men Who Stare at Goats (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1234548/?ls), [Fantastic Mr. Fox (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0432283/?ls), and [Jason Reitman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0718646/?ls)'s [Up in the Air (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1193138/?ls). Clooney received critical acclaim for his performance in Up in the Air (2009) and was nominated for several awards, including a Golden Globe Award and Academy Award. He didn't win that year, but took home both Best Actor awards (as well as countless nominations) for his role as a father who finds out his wife was unfaithful as she lays in a coma in [Alexander Payne](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0668247/?ls)'s [The Descendants (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1033575/?ls). Through his career, Clooney has been heralded for his political activism and humanitarian work. He has served as one of the United Nations Messengers of Peace since 2008, has been an advocate for the Darfur conflict, and organized the Hope for Haiti telethon, to raise money for the victims of the 2010 earthquake. In March 2012, Clooney was arrested for civil disobedience while protesting at the Sudanese embassy in Washington, D.C.  
  
Clooney was married to actress [Talia Balsam](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0051104/?ls), from 1989 until 1993. After their divorce, he swore he would never marry again. [Michelle Pfeiffer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000201/?ls) and [Nicole Kidman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000173/?ls) bet him $10,000 that he would have children by the age of 40, and sent him a check shortly after his birthday. Clooney returned the funds and bet double or nothing he wouldn't have children by the age of 50. Although he has remained a consummate bachelor, Clooney has had many highly publicized relationships, including with former WWE wrestler [Stacy Keibler](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0445001/?ls). In 2014, he married lawyer and activist [Amal Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5007802/?ls), with whom he has two children, twins.

Nominated twice for writing a film, first in 2006 for his original screenplay "Good Night, Good Luck" and for adapting "The Ides of March" in 2011. Clooney has won Oscars both for acting and producing a film.

Matthew Paige Damon was born on October 8, 1970, in Boston, Massachusetts, to [Kent Damon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1497320/?ls), a stockbroker, realtor and tax preparer, and [Nancy Carlsson-Paige](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1497472/?ls), an early childhood education professor at Lesley University. Matt has an older brother, Kyle, a sculptor. His father was of English and Scottish descent, and his mother is of Finnish and Swedish ancestry. The family lived in Newton until his parents divorced in 1973, when Damon and his brother moved with his mother to Cambridge. He grew up in a stable community, and was raised near actor [Ben Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000255/?ls).  
  
Damon attended Cambridge Rindge and Latin School and he performed in a number of theater productions during his time there. He attended Harvard University as an English major. While in Harvard, he kept on skipping classes to pursue acting projects, which included the TNT original film, [Rising Son (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0100497/?ls), and prep-school drama, [School Ties (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0105327/?ls). It was until his film, [Geronimo: An American Legend (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107004/?ls), was expected to be a big success that he decided to drop out of university completely. Arriving in Hollywood, Matt managed to get his first break with a part in the romantic comedy, [Mystic Pizza (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0095690/?ls). However, the film did not do too well and his film career failed to take off. Not letting failure discourage him from acting, he went for another audition, and managed to get a starring role in [School Ties (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0105327/?ls). Up next for Matt was a role as a soldier who had problems with drug-addiction in the movie, [Courage Under Fire (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115956/?ls). Matt had, in fact, lost forty pounds for his role which resulted in health problems.  
  
The following year, he garnered accolades for [Good Will Hunting (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119217/?ls), a screenplay he had originally written for an English class at Harvard University. [Good Will Hunting (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119217/?ls) was nominated for 9 Academy Awards, one of which, Matt won for Best Original Screenplay along with [Ben Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000255/?ls). In the year 1998, Matt played the title role in [Steven Spielberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000229/?ls)'s film, [Saving Private Ryan (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120815/?ls), which was one of the most acclaimed films in that year. Matt had the opportunity of working with [Tom Hanks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000158/?ls) and [Vin Diesel](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004874/?ls) while filming that movie. That same year, he starred as an earnest law student and reformed poker player in [Rounders (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0128442/?ls), starring opposite [Edward Norton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001570/?ls) and [John Malkovich](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000518/?ls). The next year, Matt rejoined his childhood friend, [Ben Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000255/?ls) and fellow comedian, [Chris Rock](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001674/?ls), in the comedy [Dogma (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120655/?ls).  
  
Towards the end of 1999, Matt played "Tom Ripley", a working-class young man who tastes the good life and will do anything to live it. Both [Jude Law](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000179/?ls) and [Gwyneth Paltrow](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000569/?ls) also starred in the movie. [The Talented Mr. Ripley (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0134119/?ls) earned mixed reviews from critics, but even so, Matt earned praise for his performance. Matt lent his voice to the animated movie, [Titan A.E. (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120913/?ls) in the year 2000, which also earned mixed reviews from the public. He also starred in two other movies, [All the Pretty Horses (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0149624/?ls) and the golf comedy-drama, [The Legend of Bagger Vance (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0146984/?ls), starring alongside [Will Smith](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000226/?ls). In the year 2003, he signed on to star in [The Informant! (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1130080/?ls) by [Steven Soderbergh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001752/?ls) and the Farrelly Brothers' [Stuck on You (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0338466/?ls).  #### [9. Ben Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000255/?ref_=ls_t_9) 

    *   Producer
    *   Actor
    *   Writer

[Argo (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1024648/?ref_=ls_knf_9)

Benjamin Géza "Ben" Affleck-Boldt was born on August 15, 1972 in Berkeley, California and raised in Cambridge, Massachusetts, to mother Chris Anne (Boldt), a school teacher, and father Timothy Byers "Tim" Affleck, a social worker. Ben has a younger brother, actor [Casey Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000729/?ls), who was born in 1975. He is of mostly English, Irish, German, and Scottish ancestry. His middle name, Géza, is after a Hungarian family friend who was a Holocaust survivor.  
  
Affleck wanted to be an actor ever since he could remember, and his first acting experience was for a Burger King commercial, when he was on the PBS mini-series, [The Voyage of the Mimi (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0124265/?ls). It was also at that age when Ben met his lifelong friend and fellow actor, [Matt Damon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000354/?ls). They played little league together and took drama classes together. Ben's teen years consisted of mainly TV movies and small television appearances including [Hands of a Stranger (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0093141/?ls) and [The Second Voyage of the Mimi (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0278695/?ls). He made his big introduction into feature films in 1993 when he was cast in [Dazed and Confused (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0106677/?ls). After that, he did mostly independent films like [Kevin Smith](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0003620/?ls)'s [Mallrats (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0113749/?ls) and [Chasing Amy (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118842/?ls) which were great for Ben's career, receiving renowned appreciation for his works at the Sundance film festival. But the success he was having in independent films didn't last much longer and things got a little shaky for Ben. He was living in an apartment with his brother Casey and friend Matt, getting tired of being turned down for the big roles in films and being given the forgettable supporting ones. Since Matt was having the same trouble, they decided to write their own script, where they could call all the shots. So, after finishing the script for [Good Will Hunting (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119217/?ls), they gave it to their agent, [Patrick Whitesell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0925877/?ls), who showed it to a few Hollywood studios, finally being accepted by Castle Rock. It was great news for the two, but Castle Rock wasn't willing to give Ben and Matt the control over the project they were hoping for. It was friend [Kevin Smith](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0003620/?ls) who took it to the head of Miramax who bought the script giving Ben and Matt the control they wanted and, in December 5, 1997, [Good Will Hunting (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119217/?ls) was released, making the two unknown actors famous. The film was nominated for 9 Academy Awards and won two, including Best Original Screenplay for Ben and Matt. The film marked Ben's breakthrough role, in which he was given for the first time the chance to choose roles instead of having to go through grueling auditions constantly.  
  
Affleck chose such roles in the blockbusters [Armageddon (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120591/?ls), [Shakespeare in Love (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0138097/?ls), and [Pearl Harbor (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0213149/?ls). In the early years of the 2000s, he also starred in the box office hits [Changing Lanes (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0264472/?ls), [The Sum of All Fears (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0164184/?ls), and [Daredevil (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0287978/?ls), as well as the disappointing comedies [Gigli (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0299930/?ls) and [Surviving Christmas (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0252028/?ls). While the mid 2000s were considered a career downturn for Affleck, he received a Golden Globe nomination for his performance in [Hollywoodland (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0427969/?ls). In the several years following, he played supporting roles, including in the films [Smokin' Aces (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0475394/?ls), [He's Just Not That Into You (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1001508/?ls), [State of Play (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0473705/?ls), and [Extract (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1225822/?ls). He ventured into directing in 2007, with the thriller [Gone Baby Gone (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0452623/?ls), which starred his brother, [Casey Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000729/?ls), and was well received. He then directed, co-wrote, and starred in [The Town (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0840361/?ls), which was named to the National Board of Review Top Ten Films of the year. For the political thriller [Argo (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1024648/?ls), which he directed and starred in, Affleck won the Golden Globe Award and BAFTA Award for Best Director, and the Academy Award, Golden Globe Award, and BAFTA Award for Best Picture (Affleck's second Oscar win).  
  
In 2014, Affleck headlined the book adaptation thriller [Gone Girl (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2267998/?ls). He starred as Bruce Wayne/Batman in the superhero film [Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2975590/?ls), [Suicide Squad (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1386697/?ls), and [Justice League (2017)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0974015/?ls). He reprised the role in [Zack Snyder's Justice League (2021)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt12361974/?ls) and [The Flash (2023)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0439572/?ls).  
  
Recently he has given praise-worthy performances in [The Way Back (2020)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8544498/?ls) as a recovering alcoholic, [The Last Duel (2021)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4244994/?ls) (notably he also co-wrote the script), and a scene-stealing golden globe nominated performance in [The Tender Bar (2021)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3108894/?ls).

Shared with pal Matt Damon for writing "Good Will Hunting". A few years later he won another Oscar for producing the Best Picture film "Argo" which he also starred in and directed.

[Much Ado About Nothing (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107616/?ref_=ls_knf_10)

Kenneth Charles Branagh was born on December 10, 1960, in Belfast, Northern Ireland, to parents William Branagh, a plumber and carpenter, and Frances (Harper), both born in 1930. He has two siblings, William Branagh, Jr. (born 1955) and [Joyce Branagh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0104309/?ls) (born 1970). When he was nine, his family escaped The Troubles by moving to Reading, Berkshire, England. At 23, Branagh joined the Royal Shakespeare Company, where he took on starring roles in "Henry V" and "Romeo and Juliet". He soon found the RSC too large and impersonal and formed his own, the Renaissance Theatre Company, which was disbanded in 1992 when he moved more fully into filmmaking. At 29, he directed [Henry V (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097499/?ls), where he also co-starred with his then-wife, [Emma Thompson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000668/?ls). The film brought him Best Actor and Best Director Oscar nominations. In 1993, he brought Shakespeare to mainstream audiences again with his hit adaptation of [Much Ado About Nothing (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107616/?ls), which featured an all-star cast that included, among others, [Denzel Washington](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000243/?ls), [Michael Keaton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000474/?ls) and [Keanu Reeves](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000206/?ls). At 30, he published his autobiography and, at 34, he directed and starred as "Victor Frankenstein" in the big-budget adaptation of [Mary Shelley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0791217/?ls)'s novel, [Mary Shelley's Frankenstein (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109836/?ls), with [Robert De Niro](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000134/?ls) as the monster himself. In 1996, Branagh wrote, directed and starred in a lavish adaptation of [Hamlet (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0116477/?ls). His superb film acting work also includes a wide range of roles such as in [Celebrity (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120533/?ls), [Wild Wild West (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120891/?ls), [The Road to El Dorado (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0138749/?ls), [Valkyrie (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0985699/?ls) and his stunning portrayal of [Laurence Olivier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000059/?ls) in [My Week with Marilyn (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1655420/?ls), where once again he offered a great performance that was also nominated for an Academy Award.

Nominated for adapting "Hamlet" to screen in 1996. Branagh is also nominated for Best Director and a Leading role for his film "Henry V" in 1989, a supporting role for "My Week with Marilyn" in 2011, and for directing a short film "Swan Song" in 1992.

 #### [12. Emma Thompson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000668/?ref_=ls_t_12) 

    *   Actress
    *   Writer
    *   Producer

[Sense and Sensibility (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114388/?ref_=ls_knf_12)

Emma Thompson was born on April 15, 1959 in Paddington, London, into a family of actors - father [Eric Thompson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0860117/?ls) and mother [Phyllida Law](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0492373/?ls), who has co-starred with Thompson in several films. Her sister, [Sophie Thompson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0860724/?ls), is an actor as well. Her father was English-born and her mother is Scottish-born. Thompson's wit was cultivated by a cheerful, clever, creative family atmosphere, and she was a popular and successful student. She attended Cambridge University, studying English Literature, and was part of the university's Footlights Group, the famous group where, previously, many of the Monty Python members had first met.  
  
Thompson graduated in 1980 and embarked on her career in entertainment, beginning with stints on BBC radio and touring with comedy shows. She soon got her first major break in television, on the comedy skit program [Alfresco (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0131158/?ls), writing and performing along with her fellow Footlights Group alums [Stephen Fry](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000410/?ls) and [Hugh Laurie](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0491402/?ls). She also worked on other TV comedy review programs in the mid-1980s, occasionally with some of her fellow Footlights alums, and often with actor [Robbie Coltrane](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001059/?ls).  
  
Thompson found herself collaborating again with Fry in 1985, this time in his stage adaptation of the play "Me and My Girl" in London's West End, in which she had a leading role, playing Sally Smith. The show was a success and she received favorable reviews, and the strength of her performance led to her casting as the lead in the BBC television miniseries [Fortunes of War (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0092353/?ls), in which Thompson and her co-star, [Kenneth Branagh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000110/?ls), play an English ex-patriate couple living in Eastern Europe as the Second World War erupts. Thompson won a BAFTA Award for her work on the program. She married Branagh in 1989, continued to work with him professionally, and formed a production company with him. In the late 80s and early 90s, she starred in a string of well-received and successful television and film productions, most notably her lead role in the Merchant-Ivory production of [Howards End (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0104454/?ls), which confirmed her ability to carry a movie on both sides of the Atlantic and appropriately showered her with trans-Atlantic honors - both an Oscar and a BAFTA award.  
  
Since then, Thompson has continued to move effortlessly between the art film world and mainstream Hollywood, though even her Hollywood roles tend to be in more up-market productions. She continues to work on television as well, but is generally very selective about which roles she takes. She writes for the screen as well, such as the screenplay for [Ang Lee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000487/?ls)'s [Sense and Sensibility (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114388/?ls), in which she also starred as Elinor Dashwood, and the teleplay adaptation of [Margaret Edson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0249682/?ls)'s acclaimed play [Wit (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0243664/?ls), in which she also starred.  
  
Thompson is known for her sophisticated, skillful, though her critics say somewhat mannered, performances, and of course for her arch wit, which she is unafraid to point at herself - she is a fearless self-satirist. Thompson and Branagh divorced in 1994, and Thompson is now married to fellow actor [Greg Wise](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0936353/?ls), who had played Willoughby in [Ang Lee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000487/?ls)'s [Sense and Sensibility (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114388/?ls). Thompson and Wise have one child, Gaia, born in 1999. She was appointed Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire at the 2018 Queen's Birthday Honours for her services to drama.

Nominated and won for adapting Jane Austens' "Sense and Sensibility" to screen in 1995.

Bradley Charles Cooper was born on January 5, 1975 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. His mother, Gloria (Campano), is of Italian descent, and worked for a local NBC station. His father, Charles John Cooper, who was of Irish descent, was a stockbroker. Immediately after Bradley graduated from the Honors English program at Georgetown University in 1997, he moved to New York City to enroll in the Masters of Fine Arts program at the Actors Studio Drama School at New School University. There, he developed his stage work, culminating with his thesis performance as John Merrick in [Bernard Pomerance](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0690052/?ls)'s "The Elephant Man", performed in New York's Circle in the Square.  
  
While still in school, Bradley began his professional career, appearing opposite [Sarah Jessica Parker](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000572/?ls) on [Sex and the City (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0159206/?ls) and on the drama series [The Beat (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0231013/?ls). His weekends were spent with LEAP (Learning through the Expanded Arts Program), a non-profit organization that teaches acting and movement to inner city school children. The summers took him all across the globe, from kayaking in British Columbia with Orca Whales to ice-climbing in the Peruvian Andes, while hosting Lonely Planet's [Treks in a Wild World (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0273027/?ls) for the Discovery Channel. Bradley had to miss his graduation ceremony from the Actors Studio in order to star in his first feature [Wet Hot American Summer (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0243655/?ls). After finishing his second feature [Bending All the Rules (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0349193/?ls), his plans to relocate to Los Angeles were delayed when [Darren Star](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0823015/?ls) hired him to star on the drama series [The $treet (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0247135/?ls).  
  
Bradley went on to win the role of young law student Gordon Pinella in [Changing Lanes (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0264472/?ls), starring [Ben Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000255/?ls) and [Samuel L. Jackson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000168/?ls), and also played Travis Paterson in [My Little Eye (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0280969/?ls). He finally decided that it was time to forgo his other New York projects and move to Los Angeles when he was cast on [Alias (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0285333/?ls). After supporting roles in [Wedding Crashers (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0396269/?ls), [Failure to Launch (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0427229/?ls), [The Comebacks (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0790804/?ls), [The Rocker (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1031969/?ls) and [Yes Man (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1068680/?ls), Cooper broke out with major roles in [He's Just Not That Into You (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1001508/?ls), [The Hangover (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1119646/?ls) and [Valentine's Day (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0817230/?ls). He co-starred in the action film [The A-Team (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0429493/?ls) and headlined the thriller film [Limitless (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1219289/?ls).  
  
Cooper received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor after starring opposite [Jennifer Lawrence](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2225369/?ls) in [David O. Russell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0751102/?ls)'s [Silver Linings Playbook (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1045658/?ls). He then received two more consecutive Oscar nominations, Best Supporting Actor for playing Richie DiMaso in Russell's [American Hustle (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1800241/?ls) (again opposite Lawrence, though their characters shared no significant screen time), and Best Actor for playing Navy SEAL Chris Kyle in [Clint Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000142/?ls)'s [American Sniper (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2179136/?ls), the highest grossing film of 2014. During this time period, Cooper also reprised his role in [The Hangover Part II (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1411697/?ls) and [The Hangover Part III (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1951261/?ls), turned in another strong dramatic turn in [The Place Beyond the Pines (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1817273/?ls), and voiced Rocket Raccoon in the third highest grossing film of 2014, [Guardians of the Galaxy (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2015381/?ls).  
  
In 2015, Bradley headlined two comedies, [Cameron Crowe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001081/?ls)'s [Aloha (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1243974/?ls), set in Hawaii, and [John Wells](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0920274/?ls)' [Burnt (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2503944/?ls), set in London, and starred opposite Jennifer Lawrence again in David O. Russell's [Joy (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2446980/?ls).

Greta Gerwig is an American actress, playwright, screenwriter, and director. She has collaborated with Noah Baumbach on several films, including Greenberg (2010), Frances Ha (2012), for which she earned a Golden Globe nomination, and Mistress America (2015). Gerwig made her solo directorial debut with the critically acclaimed comedy-drama film [Lady Bird (2017)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4925292/?ls), which she also wrote, and has also had starring roles in the films Damsels in Distress (2011), Jackie (2016), and 20th Century Women (2016).  
  
Greta Celeste Gerwig was born in Sacramento, California, to [Christine Gerwig](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5668279/?ls) (née Sauer), a nurse, and [Gordon Gerwig](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5668379/?ls), a financial consultant and computer programmer. She has German, Irish, and English ancestry. Gerwig was raised as a Unitarian Universalist, but also attended an all-girls Catholic school. She has described herself as "an intense child". With an early interest in dance, she intended to get a degree in musical theatre in New York. She graduated from Barnard College in NY, where she studied English and philosophy, instead. Originally intending to become a playwright, after meeting young film director [Joe Swanberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1846132/?ls), she became the star of a series of intellectual low budget movies made by first-time filmmakers, a trend dubbed "mumblecore".  
  
Gerwig was cast in a minor role in Swanberg's [LOL (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0462392/?ls) in 2006, while still studying at Barnard. She then appeared in many of Swanberg's films, and personally co-directed, co-wrote and co-produced one entitled [Nights and Weekends (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1186248/?ls). She has worked with good quality directors such as [Ti West](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1488800/?ls) ([The House of the Devil (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1172994/?ls)), [Whit Stillman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001775/?ls) ([Damsels in Distress (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1667307/?ls)), or [Woody Allen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000095/?ls) ([To Rome with Love (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1859650/?ls)) but success and (international) recognition did not come until [Frances Ha (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2347569/?ls), directed by [Noah Baumbach](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000876/?ls), a film she also co-wrote. Both tall and immature, awkward and graceful, blundering and candid, annoying and engaging, Greta has won all hearts in the title role of Frances Ha(liday).  
  
In 2017, she wrote and directed the highly acclaimed, semi-autobiographical teen movie [Lady Bird (2017)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4925292/?ls), set in 2002-2003, and starring [Saoirse Ronan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1519680/?ls), [Laurie Metcalf](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0582418/?ls), and [Timothée Chalamet](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3154303/?ls).  
  
In 2011, Gerwig received an award for Acting from the Athena Film Festival for her artistry as one of Hollywood's definitive screen actresses of her generation.

He attended West Windsor-Plainsboro High School and then transferred to the Hun School of Princeton and it was while he was there that he began taking acting classes at the McCarter Theatre on the Princeton campus. His early ambition had been to be a writer, but as a result of the acting lessons and appearances in student productions he persuaded his mother to allow him to attend an audition for a role in a sci-fi adolescent adventure, [Explorers (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0089114/?ls). He was admitted to the prestigious Carnegie-Mellon University to study theatre but his studies were interrupted when he won his break-through role opposite [Robin Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000245/?ls) in [Dead Poets Society (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097165/?ls) and he did not complete his degree. His subsequent acting career was a mix of theatre work (earning a number of awards and nominations, including a Tony Award nomination for his role in "The Coast of Utopia" at the Lincoln Center in New York), and a mix of serious and more commercial movies, notably [Gattaca (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119177/?ls) (where he met his first wife, [Uma Thurman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000235/?ls)) and [Training Day (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0139654/?ls). Meanwhile, he also wrote two novels: "The Hottest State" (1996) and "Ash Wednesday" (2002).

As a Groundlings alumna, she joins the ranks of such SNL cast mates as [Maya Rudolph](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0748973/?ls), [Will Ferrell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002071/?ls), [Phil Hartman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0367005/?ls), and [Jon Lovitz](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001484/?ls).  
  
Wiig made her big-screen debut to universal high praise as [Katherine Heigl](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001337/?ls)'s passive-aggressive boss in [Judd Apatow](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0031976/?ls)'s smash-hit comedy [Knocked Up (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0478311/?ls). Additional film credits include [Drew Barrymore](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000106/?ls)'s directorial debut, [Whip It (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1172233/?ls) starring [Elliot Page](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0680983/?ls); [Greg Mottola](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0609549/?ls)'s [Adventureland (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1091722/?ls), with [Ryan Reynolds](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005351/?ls), [Kristen Stewart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0829576/?ls), and [Jesse Eisenberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0251986/?ls); [David Koepp](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0462895/?ls)'s [Ghost Town (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0995039/?ls) with [Ricky Gervais](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0315041/?ls); and [Jake Kasdan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0440458/?ls)'s [Walk Hard: The Dewey Cox Story (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0841046/?ls), another Apatow-produced film, in which she starred opposite [John C. Reilly](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000604/?ls). She has also guest-starred on the Emmy-winning NBC series [30 Rock (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0496424/?ls), the HBO series [Bored to Death (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1255913/?ls) with [Jason Schwartzman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005403/?ls), and [Flight of the Conchords (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0863046/?ls).  
  
Wiig joined the cast of [Saturday Night Live (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072562/?ls) in 2005, and was known for playing such memorable characters as the excitable Target clerk, Lawrence Welk singer Doonese, the hilarious one-upper Penelope, House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, and Suze Orman, among others. Wiig earned four Emmy nominations for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series for her work on the show. She left the show in the spring of 2012.  
  
In 2011, Wiig co-wrote and starred in [Bridesmaids (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1478338/?ls), along with [Melissa McCarthy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0565250/?ls), [Maya Rudolph](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0748973/?ls), and [Rose Byrne](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0126284/?ls). Wiig also appeared in such notable films as [Greg Mottola](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0609549/?ls)'s [Paul (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1092026/?ls), opposite [Simon Pegg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0670408/?ls) and [Nick Frost](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0296545/?ls); [Andrew Jarecki](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1285613/?ls)'s [All Good Things (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1175709/?ls), opposite [Ryan Gosling](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0331516/?ls), [Kirsten Dunst](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000379/?ls), and [Frank Langella](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001449/?ls); DreamWorks Animation's [How to Train Your Dragon (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0892769/?ls), with [Gerard Butler](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0124930/?ls) and [Jay Baruchel](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0059431/?ls); the Universal Pictures' animated feature film [Despicable Me (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1323594/?ls), starring [Steve Carell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0136797/?ls) and [Jason Segel](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0781981/?ls); and [Jennifer Westfeldt](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0922724/?ls)'s [Friends with Kids (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1720616/?ls), opposite [Jon Hamm](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0358316/?ls), [Megan Fox](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1083271/?ls), [Adam Scott](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004395/?ls), [Maya Rudolph](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0748973/?ls) and Westfeldt.

 #### [5. George Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000123/?ref_=ls_t_5) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[The Ides of March (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1124035/?ref_=ls_knf_5)

George Timothy Clooney was born on May 6, 1961, in Lexington, Kentucky, to [Nina Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm6460343/?ls) (née Nina Bruce Warren), a beauty pageant queen, and [Nick Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0167040/?ls), a former anchorman and television host (who was also the brother of singer [Rosemary Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0167041/?ls)). He has Irish, English, and German ancestry. Clooney spent most of his youth in Ohio and Kentucky, and graduated from Augusta High School. He was very active in sports such as basketball and baseball, and tried out for the Cincinnati Reds, but was not offered a contract.  
  
After his cousin, [Miguel Ferrer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001208/?ls), got him a small role in a feature film, Clooney began to pursue acting. His first major role was on the sitcom [E/R (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086704/?ls) as Ace. More roles soon followed, including George Burnett, the handsome handyman on [The Facts of Life (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078610/?ls); Booker Brooks, a supervisor on [Roseanne (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094540/?ls); and Detective James Falconer on [Sisters (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101199/?ls). Clooney had his breakthrough when he was cast as Dr. Doug Ross on the award-winning drama series [ER (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108757/?ls), opposite [Anthony Edwards](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000381/?ls), [Noah Wyle](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001864/?ls) and [Julianna Margulies](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000523/?ls).  
  
While filming "ER" (1994), Clooney starred in a number of high profile film roles, such as [Robert Rodriguez](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001675/?ls)'s [From Dusk Till Dawn (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0116367/?ls), and [One Fine Day (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117247/?ls), opposite [Michelle Pfeiffer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000201/?ls). In 1997, Clooney took on the role of Batman in [Joel Schumacher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001708/?ls)'s [Batman & Robin (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118688/?ls). The film was a moderate success in the box office, but was slammed by critics, notably for the nipple-laden Batsuit. Clooney went on to star in [Steven Soderbergh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001752/?ls)'s [Out of Sight (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120780/?ls), [Terrence Malick](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000517/?ls)'s [The Thin Red Line (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120863/?ls), and [David O. Russell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0751102/?ls)'s [Three Kings (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120188/?ls).  
  
In 1999, Clooney left "ER" (1994) (though he would return for the season finale) and appeared in a number of films, including [O Brother, Where Art Thou? (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0190590/?ls), [The Perfect Storm (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0177971/?ls) and [Ocean's Eleven (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0240772/?ls). Collaborating once again with [Steven Soderbergh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001752/?ls), Ocean's Eleven (2001) received critical acclaim, earned more than $450 million at the box office, and spawned two sequels: [Ocean's Twelve (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0349903/?ls) and [Ocean's Thirteen (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0496806/?ls).  
  
In 2002, Clooney made his directorial debut with [Confessions of a Dangerous Mind (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0270288/?ls), an adaptation of TV producer [Chuck Barris](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0057567/?ls)' autobiography. This was the first film under the banner of Section Eight Productions, a production company he founded with [Steven Soderbergh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001752/?ls). The company also produced many acclaimed films, including [Far from Heaven (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0297884/?ls), [Syriana (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0365737/?ls), [A Scanner Darkly (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405296/?ls) and [Good Night, and Good Luck. (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0433383/?ls). Clooney won his first Oscar for Best Supporting Actor in Syriana (2005), and was nominated for Best Director and Best Original Screenplay for Good Night, and Good Luck. (2005).  
  
In 2006, Section Eight Productions was shut down so that Soderbergh could concentrate on directing, and Clooney founded a new production company, Smokehouse Productions, with his friend and longtime business partner, [Grant Heslov](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0381416/?ls).  
  
Clooney went on to produce and star in [Michael Clayton (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0465538/?ls) (which earned him an Oscar nomination for Best Actor), directed and starred in [Leatherheads (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0379865/?ls), and took leading roles in [Burn After Reading (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0887883/?ls), [The Men Who Stare at Goats (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1234548/?ls), [Fantastic Mr. Fox (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0432283/?ls), and [Jason Reitman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0718646/?ls)'s [Up in the Air (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1193138/?ls). Clooney received critical acclaim for his performance in Up in the Air (2009) and was nominated for several awards, including a Golden Globe Award and Academy Award. He didn't win that year, but took home both Best Actor awards (as well as countless nominations) for his role as a father who finds out his wife was unfaithful as she lays in a coma in [Alexander Payne](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0668247/?ls)'s [The Descendants (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1033575/?ls). Through his career, Clooney has been heralded for his political activism and humanitarian work. He has served as one of the United Nations Messengers of Peace since 2008, has been an advocate for the Darfur conflict, and organized the Hope for Haiti telethon, to raise money for the victims of the 2010 earthquake. In March 2012, Clooney was arrested for civil disobedience while protesting at the Sudanese embassy in Washington, D.C.  
  
Clooney was married to actress [Talia Balsam](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0051104/?ls), from 1989 until 1993. After their divorce, he swore he would never marry again. [Michelle Pfeiffer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000201/?ls) and [Nicole Kidman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000173/?ls) bet him $10,000 that he would have children by the age of 40, and sent him a check shortly after his birthday. Clooney returned the funds and bet double or nothing he wouldn't have children by the age of 50. Although he has remained a consummate bachelor, Clooney has had many highly publicized relationships, including with former WWE wrestler [Stacy Keibler](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0445001/?ls). In 2014, he married lawyer and activist [Amal Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5007802/?ls), with whom he has two children, twins.

Nominated twice for writing a film, first in 2006 for his original screenplay "Good Night, Good Luck" and for adapting "The Ides of March" in 2011. Clooney has won Oscars both for acting and producing a film.

Self-proclaimed troublemaker Owen Cunningham Wilson was born in Dallas, to Irish-American parents originally from Massachusetts. He grew up in Texas with his mother, Laura (Cunningham), a photographer; his father, Robert Andrew Wilson, an ad exec; and his brothers, [Andrew Wilson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0932992/?ls) (the eldest) and [Luke Wilson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005561/?ls) (the youngest). Expelled from St. Mark's School of Texas (Dallas, TX) in the tenth grade, Wilson finished his sophomore year at Thomas Jefferson School and then headed to a military academy in New Mexico. He then attended the University of Texas at Austin, where he met his future mentor and friend, [Wes Anderson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0027572/?ls). They wrote a screenplay, [Bottle Rocket (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115734/?ls), and sent it to their family friend, screenwriter [L.M. Kit Carson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0141281/?ls), who sent it to producer [Polly Platt](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0686895/?ls), who gave it to [James L. Brooks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000985/?ls), who gave the Texans $5 million to make it into a feature film. Despite critical praise, [Bottle Rocket (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115734/?ls) only grossed one million dollars. After making the film, Wilson moved to Hollywood, setting up house with his two brothers and Anderson. Fairly quickly, Owen found himself acting in a series of big budget films, such as [The Cable Guy (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115798/?ls), [The Haunting (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0171363/?ls), [Anaconda (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118615/?ls) and [Breakfast of Champions (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120618/?ls). This led to more work, such as [Shanghai Noon (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0184894/?ls), [Meet the Parents (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0212338/?ls) and [Behind Enemy Lines (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0159273/?ls). He's known not only for his nose, which has been broken several times, but also for his 'free wheeling ways' with a script. He co-wrote the film [The Royal Tenenbaums (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0265666/?ls) with his oft partner [Wes Anderson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0027572/?ls).
