**Kristen Anne Bell** (born July 18, 1980) is an American actress and singer. [Her work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Kristen_Bell_performances "List of Kristen Bell performances") includes both film and television, and [her accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Kristen_Bell "List of awards and nominations received by Kristen Bell") include two [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards"), in addition to nominations for three [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"). In 2025, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ included her in their selection of [the 100 most influential people in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-1)

Bell began her acting career starring in stage productions, while attending the [Tisch School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_School_of_the_Arts "Tisch School of the Arts") at [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University"). She made her [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") stage debut as [Becky Thatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Becky_Thatcher "Becky Thatcher") in the comedy musical _[The Adventures of Tom Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Tom\_Sawyer\_(musical) "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (musical)")_ (2001) and appeared in a Broadway revival of _[The Crucible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crucible "The Crucible")_ (2002). She then appeared in the action film _[Spartan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartan\_(film) "Spartan (film)")_ and received praise for her performance in the television drama film _[Gracie's Choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracie's\_Choice "Gracie's Choice")_ (both 2004).

Bell had her [breakout performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakthrough_role "Breakthrough role") as [the title character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Mars_(character) "Veronica Mars (character)") in the television series _[Veronica Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica\_Mars "Veronica Mars")_ (2004–2007), a role she reprised in the [2014 spin-off film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Mars_(film) "Veronica Mars (film)") and the [2019 revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Mars_(season_4) "Veronica Mars (season 4)"). She also starred as [Elle Bishop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elle_Bishop "Elle Bishop") in the superhero drama series _[Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroes\_(American\_TV\_series) "Heroes (American TV series)")_ (2007–2008), voiced the titular narrator in the teen drama series _[Gossip Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gossip\_Girl "Gossip Girl")_ (2007–2012) and its [2021 standalone sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gossip_Girl_(2021_TV_series) "Gossip Girl (2021 TV series)"), and starred in the [Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showtime_(TV_network) "Showtime (TV network)") comedy series _[House of Lies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House\_of\_Lies "House of Lies")_ (2012–2016). She received nominations for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_-_Television_Series_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress - Television Series Musical or Comedy") for her leading roles in the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") comedy series _[The Good Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Good\_Place "The Good Place")_ (2016–2020) and the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") romantic comedy series _[Nobody Wants This](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobody\_Wants\_This "Nobody Wants This")_ (2024); the latter also earned her two [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award") nominations, for [Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Lead_Actress_in_a_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series") and [Outstanding Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series").

During her time on _Veronica Mars_, Bell starred in the television musical film _[Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reefer\_Madness:\_The\_Movie\_Musical "Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical")_ (2005) and the horror film _[Pulse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulse\_(2006\_film) "Pulse (2006 film)")_ (2006). She has since appeared in a number of comedy films, including _[Forgetting Sarah Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forgetting\_Sarah\_Marshall "Forgetting Sarah Marshall")_ (2008), _[Couples Retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couples\_Retreat "Couples Retreat")_ (2009), _[When in Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_in\_Rome\_(2010\_film) "When in Rome (2010 film)")_ (2010), _[You Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Again "You Again")_ (2010), _[Burlesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlesque\_(2010\_American\_film) "Burlesque (2010 American film)")_ (2010), _[Safety Not Guaranteed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety\_Not\_Guaranteed "Safety Not Guaranteed")_ (2012), _[Stuck in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuck\_in\_Love\_(film) "Stuck in Love (film)")_ (2012), _[The Lifeguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lifeguard "The Lifeguard")_ (2013), _[The Boss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boss\_(2016\_film) "The Boss (2016 film)")_ (2016), _[Bad Moms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Moms "Bad Moms")_ (2016), _[A Bad Moms Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Bad\_Moms\_Christmas "A Bad Moms Christmas")_ (2017), _[How to Be a Latin Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How\_to\_Be\_a\_Latin\_Lover "How to Be a Latin Lover")_ (2017), _[CHiPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CHiPs\_(film) "CHiPs (film)")_ (2017), _[Like Father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like\_Father "Like Father")_ (2018), _[Queenpins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queenpins "Queenpins")_ (2021), _[The People We Hate at the Wedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_People\_We\_Hate\_at\_the\_Wedding "The People We Hate at the Wedding")_ (2022), and _[Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paw\_Patrol:\_The\_Mighty\_Movie "Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie")_ (2023). She received further recognition for voicing [Princess Anna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_(Frozen) "Anna (Frozen)") in the Disney animated films _[Frozen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen\_(2013\_film) "Frozen (2013 film)")_ (2013) and _[Frozen 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen\_2 "Frozen 2")_ (2019). She is also the voice of [Amy Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Rose "Amy Rose") in the upcoming _[Sonic the Hedgehog 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonic\_the\_Hedgehog\_4\_(film) "Sonic the Hedgehog 4 (film)")_.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Kristen Anne Bell was born on July 18, 1980, in [Huntington Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan "Huntington Woods, Michigan"), a suburb of [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-2) Her mother, Lorelei Jo ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Frygier), was a registered nurse, and her father, Thomas Michael "Tom" Bell, was a television news director.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-peoplebio-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-CBSSacramento-Father-Irma-2017-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-rft1-5)

Kristen described her mother as "very religious," which put a strain on their relationship.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-people-maron-6) Her mother is of Polish descent, and her father has German, Scottish, and Irish ancestry.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-7) Her parents divorced when she was six months old; both have remarried, and Bell has two half-sisters from her father's second marriage and four step-siblings from her mother's second marriage.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-unionfilms-8)

At the age of four, Bell said she did not like her first name, so her mother encouraged her to use her middle name, Anne, which she continued to use until high school.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-9) Just before her first year of high school, Bell's parents removed her from the public school system.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Mars-10) She attended [Shrine Catholic High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_Catholic_High_School "Shrine Catholic High School") in nearby [Royal Oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Oak,_Michigan "Royal Oak, Michigan"), where she participated in the drama and music clubs.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-11)

Before Shrine Catholic, she was a student at Burton Elementary School in Huntington Woods.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-unionfilms-8)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-12) At Shrine, she won the starring role in the school's 1997 production of _[The Wizard of Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wizard\_of\_Oz\_(1987\_musical) "The Wizard of Oz (1987 musical)")_ as [Dorothy Gale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Gale "Dorothy Gale") and appeared in productions of _[Fiddler on the Roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiddler\_on\_the\_Roof "Fiddler on the Roof")_ (1995), _[Lady, Be Good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady,\_Be\_Good\_(musical) "Lady, Be Good (musical)")_ (1996), and _[Li'l Abner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li'l\_Abner\_(musical) "Li'l Abner (musical)")_ (1998). In 1998, the year she graduated, she was named the yearbook's "Best Looking Lil' Lady" via a senior class vote.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Saturday-13)

Shortly after high school, Bell moved to [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan") to attend [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University")'s [Tisch School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_School_of_the_Arts "Tisch School of the Arts"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Ask-14) studying [musical theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theater "Musical theater"). She left about six credits shy of graduating to play a role in a Broadway musical, saying in an interview with [iVillage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IVillage "IVillage"), "You get to the point where you don't need a degree to be an actor."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Tough-15)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1992–2003: Early work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1992–2003: Early work")]

In 1992, Bell went to her first audition and won a dual role as a banana and a tree[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Star-16) in a suburban Detroit theater's production of _[Raggedy Ann and Andy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raggedy\_Ann\_and\_Andy "Raggedy Ann and Andy")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Ask-14) Her mother had established her with an agent before Bell was 13, which allowed her to appear in newspaper advertisements for several Detroit retailers and television commercials. She began private acting lessons.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Ask-14) In 1998, she had an uncredited role in the film _[Polish Wedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish\_Wedding "Polish Wedding")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-unionfilms-8) In 2001, Bell left New York University to play [Becky Thatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tom_Sawyer_characters#Becky_Thatcher "List of Tom Sawyer characters") in the short-lived Broadway musical of _[The Adventures of Tom Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Tom\_Sawyer\_(musical) "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (musical)")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-17) That year, she made her credited film debut in _[Pootie Tang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pootie\_Tang "Pootie Tang")_. Her single line of dialogue was cut, and she appears only during the credits.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-UGO-18)

In 2002, she appeared in the Broadway revival of _[The Crucible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crucible "The Crucible")_ with [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson"), [Angela Bettis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Bettis "Angela Bettis") and [Laura Linney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Linney "Laura Linney"). Bell moved to Los Angeles in 2002 because of her friendship with writers [Kevin Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Murphy_(screenwriter) "Kevin Murphy (screenwriter)") and Dan Studney,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-UGO-18) and appeared in a handful of television shows as a special guest, finding trouble gaining a recurring role in a television series. Bell said she "tested like eight times and booked nothing and every show [she] tested for got picked up", including auditions for _[Skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin\_(American\_TV\_series) "Skin (American TV series)")_ and what she called ["that Norm Macdonald show"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Minute_with_Stan_Hooper "A Minute with Stan Hooper").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Star-16) In 2003, Bell appeared in FX's _The Shield_, season 2, episode 1, which aired on January 7, 2003. She appeared in _Everwood_, season 2 episode 2 as a cheerleader. She co-starred in the film _The King and Queen of Moonlight Bay_ as Alison, a 17-year-old girl who travels to Arizona to reconnect with the father who abandoned her family.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-19)

### 2004–2006: _Veronica Mars_ and other roles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2004–2006: Veronica Mars and other roles")]

In 2004, Bell earned acclaim for her starring role in the [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") television film _[Gracie's Choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracie's\_Choice "Gracie's Choice")_, which received one of the network's highest ratings.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Tough-15) She made her debut in a theatrically released film with [David Mamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Mamet "David Mamet")'s action thriller _[Spartan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartan\_(film) "Spartan (film)")_, as Laura Newton, the kidnapped daughter of the U.S. president, acting alongside [Val Kilmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val_Kilmer "Val Kilmer").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-20) Bell guest-starred on the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") period drama series _[Deadwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadwood\_(TV\_series) "Deadwood (TV series)")_, in a two-episode story arc ("[Bullock Returns to the Camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullock_Returns_to_the_Camp_(Deadwood_episode) "Bullock Returns to the Camp (Deadwood episode)")" and "[Suffer the Little Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suffer_the_Little_Children_(Deadwood_episode) "Suffer the Little Children (Deadwood episode)")").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-21)

[![Image 6: Head and shoulders shot of wide-eyed, young blond woman smiling into the camera.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Kristen_Bell_as_Veronica_Mars_2.jpg/250px-Kristen_Bell_as_Veronica_Mars_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kristen_Bell_as_Veronica_Mars_2.jpg)

Bell on the set of _Veronica Mars_ in 2004

At 24, she won the role of the title character in the [UPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPN "UPN") noir drama series _[Veronica Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica\_Mars "Veronica Mars")_, which was launched in the fall of 2004. Created by [Rob Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Thomas_(writer) "Rob Thomas (writer)"), the series starred Bell as the seventeen-year-old anti-establishment high school student and private detective. Bell drew on the parallels between the character of Veronica and her own life, since Bell's parents had divorced and her best friend had also died.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Tough-15) The series earned acclaim from critics. Bell's performance earned her the [Saturn Award for Best Actress on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Award_for_Best_Actress_on_Television "Saturn Award for Best Actress on Television") and a nomination for the [TCA Award for Individual Achievement in Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TCA_Award_for_Individual_Achievement_in_Drama "TCA Award for Individual Achievement in Drama"), among numerous others. Some critics asserted that her performance was overlooked, and deserved consideration for a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-24)

Aside from working on _Veronica Mars_, Bell starred in _[Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reefer\_Madness:\_The\_Movie\_Musical "Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical")_, reprising the role she played in the short-lived 2001 [Off-Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Off-Broadway "Off-Broadway") musical. The musical was a spoof of _[Reefer Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reefer\_Madness "Reefer Madness")_, the 1936 exploitation film. _Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical_ debuted on the [Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showtime_(TV_network) "Showtime (TV network)") network on April 16, 2005. Also in April, Bell starred as Gracie in _[Fifty Pills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifty\_Pills "Fifty Pills")_, an entry for the [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival"). She appeared in a short independent film called _The Receipt_ and the horror film _Roman_, which was directed by her _Crucible_ co-star Angela Bettis. Released on August 11, 2006, _[Pulse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulse\_(2006\_film) "Pulse (2006 film)")_ starred Bell as the lead Mattie. A remake of the Japanese horror film _[Kairo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulse\_(2001\_film) "Pulse (2001 film)")_, the film grossed US$27.9 million worldwide[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-25) but garnered negative response from critics. Frank Scheck of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ commented, "despite the starring presence of Kristen Bell, [the] young actress has far less interesting material to work with here than she does as [the character] 'Veronica Mars.'"[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Pulse-26)

### 2007–2011: Film breakthrough and _Gossip Girl_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2007–2011: Film breakthrough and Gossip Girl")]

_Veronica Mars_ continued on UPN for a second season; for the third season, the show was renewed and appeared on the newly created [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW"). On January 19, 2007, CW Entertainment President [Dawn Ostroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawn_Ostroff "Dawn Ostroff") announced that while she was pleased with the gradual improvement of _Veronica Mars_'s ratings, the series would be put on hiatus after February sweeps to air a new reality series, _[Pussycat Dolls Present](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pussycat\_Dolls\_Present:\_The\_Search\_for\_the\_Next\_Doll "Pussycat Dolls Present: The Search for the Next Doll")_. On May 17, 2007, Ostroff announced the cancelation of the series.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Finale-27)[_[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving\_a\_source "Help:Archiving a source")_] A two-hour series finale aired in the United States on May 22, 2007, and on June 11, 2007, Thomas officially announced in an email to _[TV Guide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TV\_Guide "TV Guide")_'s Michael Ausiello that _Veronica Mars_ had been canceled by The CW.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-28) A _Veronica Mars_ feature film and comic book series continuation had been discussed,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-29) and for a short time there was talk of another collaboration between Bell and creator Thomas that would be unrelated to the _Veronica Mars_ series.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Finale-27)

Following the cancellation of _Veronica Mars_, Bell voiced interest in appearing on _Heroes_ because she was a fan.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-scifi-30) On July 29, 2007, during a train ride back to Los Angeles from [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con") with _Heroes_ actors [Zachary Quinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zachary_Quinto "Zachary Quinto") and [Masi Oka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masi_Oka "Masi Oka"), and writers from the series, the writers had mentioned that if she "ever want[ed] to come on _Heroes_, give us [writers] a call," to which Bell said she would "love to".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-TV_guide-31) Meanwhile, there were discussions about a role on _[Lost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost\_(2004\_TV\_series) "Lost (2004 TV series)")_, but Bell turned down the role[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-EWVid-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-33) of [Charlotte Staples Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Staples_Lewis "Charlotte Staples Lewis").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-34) Bell portrayed [Elle ## Public image

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Public image")]

In 2006 and again in 2013,[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-86) Bell was selected "World's Sexiest [Vegetarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetarianism "Vegetarianism")" on [PETA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_for_the_Ethical_Treatment_of_Animals "People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals")'s yearly poll.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Veg-87) She was placed 68 on [_Maxim_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_(magazine) "Maxim (magazine)")'s 2005 "Hot 100" list,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-88) 11 in _Maxim_'s 2006 "Hot 100" list,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-89) and 46 in _Maxim_'s 2007 "Hot 100" list in which she was stated to have "single-handedly saved [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") from becoming the worst network ever".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-90) In 2006, _Maxim_ also placed Bell at the top of the "Fall TV's Criminally Sexy Investigators" List.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Veg-87) In 2008, she was ranked 59 on [AskMen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AskMen "AskMen")'s Top 99 Women of 2008 List.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-91) Reflecting on her admitted popularity with "geeks", Bell was voted the fourth-sexiest woman on TV by the staff at [_Wizard_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wizard_(magazine) "Wizard (magazine)").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-92)

Bell stated she never thought of herself as womanly because "I always play and look and act 10 years younger than I am." However, she said, "Something magical happened when I turned 25 — I looked in the mirror and was like, 'You might not get carded for an R-rated movie anymore.' Like I didn't have a little stick figure anymore."[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Complex-93) Bell has said that many of her characters are [tomboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomboy "Tomboy") because she was "not homely enough to play the [nerdy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerd "Nerd") girl and not nearly pretty enough to play the pretty girl".[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Complex-93)

[![Image 9: A blond woman wearing a green top leans forward over the table to smile at the camera to her left](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Kristen_Bell_2.jpg/250px-Kristen_Bell_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kristen_Bell_2.jpg)

Bell signing autographs in 2006 at the [Metreon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metreon "Metreon") in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco")

Bell has been associated with the idea that "[nerdy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerd "Nerd") is the new cool", and she explained, "what was previously perceived as nerdy is now viewed as original. What I like about nerdiness, [geekiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geek "Geek"), is it doesn't really matter what you're into—it just means you're not a follower."[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Complex-93) She has also said, "I love nerds. [Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic-Con_International "Comic-Con International") junkies are the tastemakers of tomorrow. Isn't that funny? The tables have turned."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-UGO-18) Vanessa Juarez of _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ commented that Bell's roles on _Veronica Mars_, _Heroes_ and as a _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ fanatic in _[Fanboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanboys\_(film) "Fanboys (film)")_ have "solidif[ied] her placement at the center of the geek universe," while [Rodney Rothman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Rothman "Rodney Rothman") stated, "I guess she's cornered the market on losers."[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-94) Bell's work is often compared to [Sarah Michelle Gellar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Michelle_Gellar "Sarah Michelle Gellar")'s portrayal of the [title character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffy_Summers "Buffy Summers") on the television series _[Buffy the Vampire Slayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffy\_the\_Vampire\_Slayer "Buffy the Vampire Slayer")_.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Bianco--95) Frank Scheck of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ stated that Bell was "arguably the television successor [to Gellar's portrayal of Buffy] when it comes to fighting bad guys." Bell is sometimes confused with [Lauren Conrad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauren_Conrad "Lauren Conrad") from _[The Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hills\_(TV\_series) "The Hills (TV series)")_. "Yeah, sometimes fans yell, 'Hey, Lauren' to me, but usually from a distance," said Bell.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Pulse-26)

Despite "new celebrity" status, Bell claimed that she was not concerned because "no one ever recognizes me anyway". She has said that her friend [Hayden Panettiere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayden_Panettiere "Hayden Panettiere") is more famous than she is and attracts more attention; as Bell explained, "I hang out with Hayden quite a bit—they never take pictures of me. I just step to the side, and I push myself in front of her when she wants to get out of it, or put her in the car."[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Complex-93)

Bell was a recurring guest on _[The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Late\_Late\_Show\_with\_Craig\_Ferguson "The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson")_, appearing in interviews as well as sketches. On _The Late Late Show_, she repeatedly showed a humorous hostility towards [Craig Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Ferguson "Craig Ferguson")'s robot skeleton sidekick [Geoff Peterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Peterson "Geoff Peterson"), claiming that she had wanted to be Ferguson's sidekick on his show and taking it upon herself to cut Peterson down every chance she got. Both Bell and Peterson appeared with Ferguson during the five _Late Late Show_ episodes filmed in France in 2011.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-96)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Personal life")]

### Relationships and family

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Relationships and family")]

[![Image 11: Photo of Dax Shepard and Kristen Bell, where Shepard is a head taller, Bell is wearing a multi-colored dress](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/Kristen_Bell%2C_Dax_Shepard_2012.jpg/250px-Kristen_Bell%2C_Dax_Shepard_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kristen_Bell,_Dax_Shepard_2012.jpg)

[Dax Shepard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dax_Shepard "Dax Shepard") and Bell at the 2012 [DoSomething](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoSomething "DoSomething") Awards

In 2007, Bell ended a five-year relationship with former fiancé Kevin Mann.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-102) She later told _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex\_(magazine) "Complex (magazine)")_ magazine that dating "makes me want to vomit. And not out of grossness—OK, a little bit out of grossness, but just nerves... I've always been a [serial monogamist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serial_monogamy "Serial monogamy")."[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Complex-93)

In late 2007, Bell began dating actor [Dax Shepard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dax_Shepard "Dax Shepard"), who is also from the [Detroit metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Detroit "Metro Detroit"). They announced their engagement in January 2010.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-103) They decided to delay marriage until the state of California passed legislation legalizing [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-104) They co-starred in the 2010 film _[When in Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_in\_Rome\_(2010\_film) "When in Rome (2010 film)")_, the 2012 film _[Hit and Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit\_and\_Run\_(2012\_film) "Hit and Run (2012 film)")_,[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-105) and the 2017 film _[CHiPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CHiPs\_(film) "CHiPs (film)")_. After section 3 of the [Defense of Marriage Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_of_Marriage_Act "Defense of Marriage Act") was ruled unconstitutional by the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Supreme_Court "U.S. Supreme Court") on June 26, 2013, Bell asked Shepard to marry her through Twitter,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Twitter-KristenProp-2013-106) which he accepted.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-DaxProp-2013-107) They were married at the [Beverly Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California") County Clerk's Office on October 16, 2013.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-108) They have two daughters, born in March 2013 and December 2014.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-110)

### Mental health

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Mental health")]

In May 2016, Bell said that she has received treatment for [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depression_(mood) "Depression (mood)") and [anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety_disorder "Anxiety disorder").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-111) She said, "It's important for me to be candid about this so people in a similar situation can realize that they are not worthless and that they do have something to offer."[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-112) In a March 2020 blog post, Bell wrote, "Don't be fooled by this game of perfection that humans play. Because Instagram and magazines and TV shows, they strive for a certain aesthetic, and everything looks so beautiful, and people seem like they don't have any problems, but everyone's human. Everyone has problems. Everyone feels yucky on the inside sometimes."[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-113)

In an interview with [Jimmy Kimmel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Kimmel "Jimmy Kimmel") in August 2018, Bell discussed why she wears scuba gloves while swimming. She stated that she fears the sensation of touching things with water-immersed, wrinkled fingers, otherwise known as "[prune fingers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prune_fingers "Prune fingers")". The gloves have allowed her to swim with her children without fearing touching them.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-114)

### Beliefs and interests

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Beliefs and interests")]

[![Image 12: Photo of Kristen Bell wearing a light hat fedora hat, resting her left hand on the neck of a light brown dog](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Kristen_Bell_2012.jpg/250px-Kristen_Bell_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kristen_Bell_2012.jpg)

Bell with the Dancing Merengue Dog at the [2012 Bonnaroo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Bonnaroo_Music_Festival "2012 Bonnaroo Music Festival")

At age 11, Bell became a [vegetarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetarianism "Vegetarianism").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Veg-87) In an interview with [PETA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PETA "PETA"), Bell discussed her pets, "I have always been an animal lover. I had a hard time disassociating the animals I cuddled with—dogs and cats, for example—from the animals on my plate, and I never really cared for the taste of meat. I always loved my [Brussels sprouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_sprout "Brussels sprout")!"[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-autogenerated1-115) By 2012, Bell and Shepard had become [vegan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veganism "Veganism") after watching the documentary _[Forks Over Knives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forks\_Over\_Knives "Forks Over Knives")_.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-BellDax-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-117) However, during her first pregnancy she went back to eating dairy products and eggs.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-118) She started eating meat in 2022.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-119)

Bell has said that she is [non-religious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-religious "Non-religious") and identifies as a [humanist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanism "Humanism").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-people-maron-6) She and her husband Dax Shepard are pro-[vaccination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccination "Vaccination").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-121) Bell supported and campaigned for [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") during the [2008 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election "2008 United States presidential election"). Along with [Rashida Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashida_Jones "Rashida Jones"), she visited college campuses in [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") to discuss the candidates and encourage voter registration.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-124) Bell showed support for the [Writers Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America "Writers Guild of America") in the [writers' strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike"), appearing in the picket lines in December 2007, stating, "the writers are just looking for some fairness".[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-125)

In 2023, Bell revealed that she had taken up [Brazilian jiu-jitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_jiu-jitsu "Brazilian jiu-jitsu"). She was training under Cesalina Gracie in mother-daughter classes alongside her daughter.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-126)

### Charity work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Charity work")]

During her time in Michigan, Bell fostered animals from the [Michigan Humane Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_Humane_Society "Michigan Humane Society"), and she now supports the San Diego–based [Helen Woodward Animal Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Woodward_Animal_Center "Helen Woodward Animal Center"). Bell often attends fundraisers for the [American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_for_the_Prevention_of_Cruelty_to_Animals "American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals") and other non-profit organizations dedicated to protecting animals. She has had several dogs, including a [Welsh Corgi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_Corgi "Welsh Corgi")-[Chow Chow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chow_Chow "Chow Chow") mix named Lola, a Welsh Corgi-[Chihuahua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihuahua_(dog_breed) "Chihuahua (dog breed)") mix named Shakey and a black [Labrador Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador_Retriever "Labrador Retriever") named Sadie, who was 11-years-old when she was rescued from [Hurricane Katrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Katrina "Hurricane Katrina") and adopted by Bell in 2005.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Mars-10)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-127)

Bell and other _Veronica Mars_ cast members, including [Ryan Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Hansen "Ryan Hansen"), are involved with the charity [Invisible Children, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invisible_Children,_Inc. "Invisible Children, Inc.") The goal of the organization is to create awareness of the plight of [Northern Ugandans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Uganda "Northern Uganda") who are caught in the midst of a [civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_war "Civil war") between the government and [Joseph Kony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Kony "Joseph Kony")'s [Lord's Resistance Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Resistance_Army "Lord's Resistance Army").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-LoVe-128) In 2014, Bell launched a [Prizeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prizeo "Prizeo") campaign offering fans a chance to win a date with her in return for donating to Invisible Children, Inc.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-129) In 2018, Bell participated in a television advertisement for bone marrow donations, specifically the Gift of Life Marrow Registry. Her actions resulted in several matches that are documented on the Gift of Life website.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-130) Bell won a [2020 Webby Special Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Webby_Award "2020 Webby Award").[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Kastrenakes-131)

In 2013, Kristen Bell, along with actors [Ryan Devlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Devlin "Ryan Devlin"), [Todd Grinnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Grinnell "Todd Grinnell"), and [Ravi Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravi_Patel_(actor) "Ravi Patel (actor)"), founded the granola bar company This Bar Saves Lives to help fight malnutrition. The business donates food aid in the form of nutrition packets to children in [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti"), [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan "South Sudan"), [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia"), and [Somalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia "Somalia"). Since its launch, the company has donated more than 10 million packets as of February 2019.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-132)

### Entrepreneurship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Entrepreneurship")]

In 2019, Bell and her husband founded the company Hello Bello that markets plant-based baby care products said to be environmentally friendly and affordable.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-133) As of 2021, Hello Bello's estimated annual revenue was $26.1 million a year with 104 employees.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-134) In 2020, she partnered to start Happy Dance, a line of vegan CBD products such as eye cream and hand moisturizers. In 2023, Hello Bello filed for [Chapter 11 bankruptcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapter_11_bankruptcy "Chapter 11 bankruptcy"), blaming years of declining sales and the financial startup crisis. The company is set to be acquired by private equity firm Hildred Capital Management.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-135)

**Kristen Anne Bell** (born July 18, 1980) is an American actress and singer. [Her work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Kristen_Bell_performances "List of Kristen Bell performances") includes both film and television, and [her accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Kristen_Bell "List of awards and nominations received by Kristen Bell") include two [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards"), in addition to nominations for three [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"). In 2025, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ included her in their selection of [the 100 most influential people in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-1)

Bell began her acting career starring in stage productions, while attending the [Tisch School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_School_of_the_Arts "Tisch School of the Arts") at [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University"). She made her [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") stage debut as [Becky Thatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Becky_Thatcher "Becky Thatcher") in the comedy musical _[The Adventures of Tom Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Tom\_Sawyer\_(musical) "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (musical)")_ (2001) and appeared in a Broadway revival of _[The Crucible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crucible "The Crucible")_ (2002). She then appeared in the action film _[Spartan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartan\_(film) "Spartan (film)")_ and received praise for her performance in the television drama film _[Gracie's Choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracie's\_Choice "Gracie's Choice")_ (both 2004).

Bell had her [breakout performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakthrough_role "Breakthrough role") as [the title character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Mars_(character) "Veronica Mars (character)") in the television series _[Veronica Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica\_Mars "Veronica Mars")_ (2004–2007), a role she reprised in the [2014 spin-off film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Mars_(film) "Veronica Mars (film)") and the [2019 revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica_Mars_(season_4) "Veronica Mars (season 4)"). She also starred as [Elle Bishop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elle_Bishop "Elle Bishop") in the superhero drama series _[Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroes\_(American\_TV\_series) "Heroes (American TV series)")_ (2007–2008), voiced the titular narrator in the teen drama series _[Gossip Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gossip\_Girl "Gossip Girl")_ (2007–2012) and its [2021 standalone sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gossip_Girl_(2021_TV_series) "Gossip Girl (2021 TV series)"), and starred in the [Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showtime_(TV_network) "Showtime (TV network)") comedy series _[House of Lies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House\_of\_Lies "House of Lies")_ (2012–2016). She received nominations for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_-_Television_Series_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress - Television Series Musical or Comedy") for her leading roles in the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") comedy series _[The Good Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Good\_Place "The Good Place")_ (2016–2020) and the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") romantic comedy series _[Nobody Wants This](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobody\_Wants\_This "Nobody Wants This")_ (2024); the latter also earned her two [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award") nominations, for [Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Lead_Actress_in_a_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series") and [Outstanding Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series").

During her time on _Veronica Mars_, Bell starred in the television musical film _[Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reefer\_Madness:\_The\_Movie\_Musical "Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical")_ (2005) and the horror film _[Pulse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulse\_(2006\_film) "Pulse (2006 film)")_ (2006). She has since appeared in a number of comedy films, including _[Forgetting Sarah Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forgetting\_Sarah\_Marshall "Forgetting Sarah Marshall")_ (2008), _[Couples Retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couples\_Retreat "Couples Retreat")_ (2009), _[When in Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_in\_Rome\_(2010\_film) "When in Rome (2010 film)")_ (2010), _[You Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Again "You Again")_ (2010), _[Burlesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlesque\_(2010\_American\_film) "Burlesque (2010 American film)")_ (2010), _[Safety Not Guaranteed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety\_Not\_Guaranteed "Safety Not Guaranteed")_ (2012), _[Stuck in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuck\_in\_Love\_(film) "Stuck in Love (film)")_ (2012), _[The Lifeguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lifeguard "The Lifeguard")_ (2013), _[The Boss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boss\_(2016\_film) "The Boss (2016 film)")_ (2016), _[Bad Moms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Moms "Bad Moms")_ (2016), _[A Bad Moms Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Bad\_Moms\_Christmas "A Bad Moms Christmas")_ (2017), _[How to Be a Latin Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How\_to\_Be\_a\_Latin\_Lover "How to Be a Latin Lover")_ (2017), _[CHiPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CHiPs\_(film) "CHiPs (film)")_ (2017), _[Like Father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like\_Father "Like Father")_ (2018), _[Queenpins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queenpins "Queenpins")_ (2021), _[The People We Hate at the Wedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_People\_We\_Hate\_at\_the\_Wedding "The People We Hate at the Wedding")_ (2022), and _[Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paw\_Patrol:\_The\_Mighty\_Movie "Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie")_ (2023). She received further recognition for voicing [Princess Anna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_(Frozen) "Anna (Frozen)") in the Disney animated films _[Frozen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen\_(2013\_film) "Frozen (2013 film)")_ (2013) and _[Frozen 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen\_2 "Frozen 2")_ (2019). She is also the voice of [Amy Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Rose "Amy Rose") in the upcoming _[Sonic the Hedgehog 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonic\_the\_Hedgehog\_4\_(film) "Sonic the Hedgehog 4 (film)")_.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Kristen Anne Bell was born on July 18, 1980, in [Huntington Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan "Huntington Woods, Michigan"), a suburb of [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-2) Her mother, Lorelei Jo ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Frygier), was a registered nurse, and her father, Thomas Michael "Tom" Bell, was a television news director.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-peoplebio-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-CBSSacramento-Father-Irma-2017-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-rft1-5)

Kristen described her mother as "very religious," which put a strain on their relationship.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-people-maron-6) Her mother is of Polish descent, and her father has German, Scottish, and Irish ancestry.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-7) Her parents divorced when she was six months old; both have remarried, and Bell has two half-sisters from her father's second marriage and four step-siblings from her mother's second marriage.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-unionfilms-8)

At the age of four, Bell said she did not like her first name, so her mother encouraged her to use her middle name, Anne, which she continued to use until high school.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-9) Just before her first year of high school, Bell's parents removed her from the public school system.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Mars-10) She attended [Shrine Catholic High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_Catholic_High_School "Shrine Catholic High School") in nearby [Royal Oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Oak,_Michigan "Royal Oak, Michigan"), where she participated in the drama and music clubs.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-11)

Before Shrine Catholic, she was a student at Burton Elementary School in Huntington Woods.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-unionfilms-8)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-12) At Shrine, she won the starring role in the school's 1997 production of _[The Wizard of Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wizard\_of\_Oz\_(1987\_musical) "The Wizard of Oz (1987 musical)")_ as [Dorothy Gale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Gale "Dorothy Gale") and appeared in productions of _[Fiddler on the Roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiddler\_on\_the\_Roof "Fiddler on the Roof")_ (1995), _[Lady, Be Good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady,\_Be\_Good\_(musical) "Lady, Be Good (musical)")_ (1996), and _[Li'l Abner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li'l\_Abner\_(musical) "Li'l Abner (musical)")_ (1998). In 1998, the year she graduated, she was named the yearbook's "Best Looking Lil' Lady" via a senior class vote.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Saturday-13)

Shortly after high school, Bell moved to [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan") to attend [New York University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University "New York University")'s [Tisch School of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisch_School_of_the_Arts "Tisch School of the Arts"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Ask-14) studying [musical theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theater "Musical theater"). She left about six credits shy of graduating to play a role in a Broadway musical, saying in an interview with [iVillage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IVillage "IVillage"), "You get to the point where you don't need a degree to be an actor."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Tough-15)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1992–2003: Early work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1992–2003: Early work")]

In 1992, Bell went to her first audition and won a dual role as a banana and a tree[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Star-16) in a suburban Detroit theater's production of _[Raggedy Ann and Andy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raggedy\_Ann\_and\_Andy "Raggedy Ann and Andy")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Ask-14) Her mother had established her with an agent before Bell was 13, which allowed her to appear in newspaper advertisements for several Detroit retailers and television commercials. She began private acting lessons.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Ask-14) In 1998, she had an uncredited role in the film _[Polish Wedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish\_Wedding "Polish Wedding")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-unionfilms-8) In 2001, Bell left New York University to play [Becky Thatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tom_Sawyer_characters#Becky_Thatcher "List of Tom Sawyer characters") in the short-lived Broadway musical of _[The Adventures of Tom Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Tom\_Sawyer\_(musical) "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (musical)")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-17) That year, she made her credited film debut in _[Pootie Tang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pootie\_Tang "Pootie Tang")_. Her single line of dialogue was cut, and she appears only during the credits.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-UGO-18)

In 2002, she appeared in the Broadway revival of _[The Crucible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crucible "The Crucible")_ with [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson"), [Angela Bettis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Bettis "Angela Bettis") and [Laura Linney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Linney "Laura Linney"). Bell moved to Los Angeles in 2002 because of her friendship with writers [Kevin Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Murphy_(screenwriter) "Kevin Murphy (screenwriter)") and Dan Studney,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-UGO-18) and appeared in a handful of television shows as a special guest, finding trouble gaining a recurring role in a television series. Bell said she "tested like eight times and booked nothing and every show [she] tested for got picked up", including auditions for _[Skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin\_(American\_TV\_series) "Skin (American TV series)")_ and what she called ["that Norm Macdonald show"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Minute_with_Stan_Hooper "A Minute with Stan Hooper").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Star-16) In 2003, Bell appeared in FX's _The Shield_, season 2, episode 1, which aired on January 7, 2003. She appeared in _Everwood_, season 2 episode 2 as a cheerleader. She co-starred in the film _The King and Queen of Moonlight Bay_ as Alison, a 17-year-old girl who travels to Arizona to reconnect with the father who abandoned her family.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-19)

### 2004–2006: _Veronica Mars_ and other roles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2004–2006: Veronica Mars and other roles")]

In 2004, Bell earned acclaim for her starring role in the [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") television film _[Gracie's Choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracie's\_Choice "Gracie's Choice")_, which received one of the network's highest ratings.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Tough-15) She made her debut in a theatrically released film with [David Mamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Mamet "David Mamet")'s action thriller _[Spartan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartan\_(film) "Spartan (film)")_, as Laura Newton, the kidnapped daughter of the U.S. president, acting alongside [Val Kilmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val_Kilmer "Val Kilmer").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-20) Bell guest-starred on the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") period drama series _[Deadwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadwood\_(TV\_series) "Deadwood (TV series)")_, in a two-episode story arc ("[Bullock Returns to the Camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullock_Returns_to_the_Camp_(Deadwood_episode) "Bullock Returns to the Camp (Deadwood episode)")" and "[Suffer the Little Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suffer_the_Little_Children_(Deadwood_episode) "Suffer the Little Children (Deadwood episode)")").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-21)

[![Image 6: Head and shoulders shot of wide-eyed, young blond woman smiling into the camera.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Kristen_Bell_as_Veronica_Mars_2.jpg/250px-Kristen_Bell_as_Veronica_Mars_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kristen_Bell_as_Veronica_Mars_2.jpg)

Bell on the set of _Veronica Mars_ in 2004

At 24, she won the role of the title character in the [UPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPN "UPN") noir drama series _[Veronica Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica\_Mars "Veronica Mars")_, which was launched in the fall of 2004. Created by [Rob Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Thomas_(writer) "Rob Thomas (writer)"), the series starred Bell as the seventeen-year-old anti-establishment high school student and private detective. Bell drew on the parallels between the character of Veronica and her own life, since Bell's parents had divorced and her best friend had also died.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Tough-15) The series earned acclaim from critics. Bell's performance earned her the [Saturn Award for Best Actress on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Award_for_Best_Actress_on_Television "Saturn Award for Best Actress on Television") and a nomination for the [TCA Award for Individual Achievement in Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TCA_Award_for_Individual_Achievement_in_Drama "TCA Award for Individual Achievement in Drama"), among numerous others. Some critics asserted that her performance was overlooked, and deserved consideration for a [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-24)

Aside from working on _Veronica Mars_, Bell starred in _[Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reefer\_Madness:\_The\_Movie\_Musical "Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical")_, reprising the role she played in the short-lived 2001 [Off-Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Off-Broadway "Off-Broadway") musical. The musical was a spoof of _[Reefer Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reefer\_Madness "Reefer Madness")_, the 1936 exploitation film. _Reefer Madness: The Movie Musical_ debuted on the [Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showtime_(TV_network) "Showtime (TV network)") network on April 16, 2005. Also in April, Bell starred as Gracie in _[Fifty Pills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifty\_Pills "Fifty Pills")_, an entry for the [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival"). She appeared in a short independent film called _The Receipt_ and the horror film _Roman_, which was directed by her _Crucible_ co-star Angela Bettis. Released on August 11, 2006, _[Pulse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulse\_(2006\_film) "Pulse (2006 film)")_ starred Bell as the lead Mattie. A remake of the Japanese horror film _[Kairo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulse\_(2001\_film) "Pulse (2001 film)")_, the film grossed US$27.9 million worldwide[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-25) but garnered negative response from critics. Frank Scheck of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ commented, "despite the starring presence of Kristen Bell, [the] young actress has far less interesting material to work with here than she does as [the character] 'Veronica Mars.'"[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Pulse-26)

### 2007–2011: Film breakthrough and _Gossip Girl_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2007–2011: Film breakthrough and Gossip Girl")]

_Veronica Mars_ continued on UPN for a second season; for the third season, the show was renewed and appeared on the newly created [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW"). On January 19, 2007, CW Entertainment President [Dawn Ostroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawn_Ostroff "Dawn Ostroff") announced that while she was pleased with the gradual improvement of _Veronica Mars_'s ratings, the series would be put on hiatus after February sweeps to air a new reality series, _[Pussycat Dolls Present](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pussycat\_Dolls\_Present:\_The\_Search\_for\_the\_Next\_Doll "Pussycat Dolls Present: The Search for the Next Doll")_. On May 17, 2007, Ostroff announced the cancelation of the series.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Finale-27)[_[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving\_a\_source "Help:Archiving a source")_] A two-hour series finale aired in the United States on May 22, 2007, and on June 11, 2007, Thomas officially announced in an email to _[TV Guide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TV\_Guide "TV Guide")_'s Michael Ausiello that _Veronica Mars_ had been canceled by The CW.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-28) A _Veronica Mars_ feature film and comic book series continuation had been discussed,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-29) and for a short time there was talk of another collaboration between Bell and creator Thomas that would be unrelated to the _Veronica Mars_ series.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Finale-27)

Following the cancellation of _Veronica Mars_, Bell voiced interest in appearing on _Heroes_ because she was a fan.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-scifi-30) On July 29, 2007, during a train ride back to Los Angeles from [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con") with _Heroes_ actors [Zachary Quinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zachary_Quinto "Zachary Quinto") and [Masi Oka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masi_Oka "Masi Oka"), and writers from the series, the writers had mentioned that if she "ever want[ed] to come on _Heroes_, give us [writers] a call," to which Bell said she would "love to".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-TV_guide-31) Meanwhile, there were discussions about a role on _[Lost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost\_(2004\_TV\_series) "Lost (2004 TV series)")_, but Bell turned down the role[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-EWVid-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-33) of [Charlotte Staples Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Staples_Lewis "Charlotte Staples Lewis").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-34) Bell portrayed [Elle Bishop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elle_Bishop "Elle Bishop") on _Heroes_, a "mysterious young lady" with an "awesome power".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-TV_guide-31) She did not have to audition for the role of Elle,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-UGO-18) who made her first appearance in an October 2007 episode, and appeared in twelve episodes during the run of the series.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Variety-35) The casting of Bell, _Heroes_ creator [Tim Kring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Kring "Tim Kring") explained, "was not easy to pull off", but because of the large ensemble cast of the series and multiple [story arcs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Story_arc "Story arc"), "we found a way to jump into a small window in [Bell's] schedule."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Variety-35) Bell lent her voice to The CW series _[Gossip Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gossip\_Girl "Gossip Girl")_; she voiced the titular character in every episode of the series, appearing in person only for a surprise cameo in the final episode, portraying herself.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-37)

[![Image 7: Head and shoulders of young, blond woman with hair curling below her shoulders, smiling.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Kristen_Bell_at_the_2008_Tribeca_Film_Festival.JPG/250px-Kristen_Bell_at_the_2008_Tribeca_Film_Festival.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kristen_Bell_at_the_2008_Tribeca_Film_Festival.JPG)

Bell at the 2008 [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival")

Shortly after the cancelation of _Veronica Mars_ in early 2007, Bell filmed on location in [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii") for a starring role as the title character in the [Judd Apatow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd_Apatow "Judd Apatow") comedy _[Forgetting Sarah Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forgetting\_Sarah\_Marshall "Forgetting Sarah Marshall")_. She regarded the [improvisational comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Improvisational_comedy "Improvisational comedy") in the film as "a lovely experience".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-UGO-18) The film, written by and also starring [Jason Segel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Segel "Jason Segel"), was released theatrically on April 18, 2008, and greatly increased Bell's profile. Bell lent her voice and likeness to the video game _[Assassin's Creed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassin's\_Creed\_(video\_game) "Assassin's Creed (video game)")_, which was released in November 2007 for consoles and April 2008 for the PC.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-38) Bell reprised her role of Lucy in _[Assassin's Creed II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassin's\_Creed\_II "Assassin's Creed II")_, released in November 2009, and again in _[Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassin's\_Creed:\_Brotherhood "Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood")_, released in November 2010.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-39) In the spring of 2006, she finished filming the _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_-themed comedy _[Fanboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanboys\_(film) "Fanboys (film)")_. Director [Kyle Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Newman "Kyle Newman") received additional funding to shoot new scenes, but the busy schedules of the actors only allowed for filming in September 2007. As a result, the release was delayed until January 14, 2008.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-40) Bell starred in the 2009 comedies _[Serious Moonlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serious\_Moonlight\_(2009\_film) "Serious Moonlight (2009 film)")_, alongside [Meg Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meg_Ryan "Meg Ryan"), and _[Couples Retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couples\_Retreat "Couples Retreat")_, which chronicles four couples who partake in therapy sessions at a tropical island resort. [Jason Bateman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bateman "Jason Bateman") played her husband.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-41) She provided the voice for Cora in _[Astro Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro\_Boy\_(film) "Astro Boy (film)")_. On March 31, 2008, Bell began shooting the [Mark Steven Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Steven_Johnson "Mark Steven Johnson")-written [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney") film _[When in Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_in\_Rome\_(2010\_film) "When in Rome (2010 film)")_ on location in Rome and New York; the film was released in 2010.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-42) Bell reprised her role as Sarah Marshall for a cameo appearance in the film _[Get Him to the Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get\_Him\_to\_the\_Greek "Get Him to the Greek")_, a spin-off sequel from _Forgetting Sarah Marshall_, released June 4, 2010.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-44)

Bell co-starred alongside singers [Christina Aguilera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Aguilera "Christina Aguilera") and [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher "Cher") in the backstage musical film _[Burlesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlesque\_(2010\_American\_film) "Burlesque (2010 American film)")_, which was released in November 2010. ## Public image

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Public image")]

In 2006 and again in 2013,[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-86) Bell was selected "World's Sexiest [Vegetarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetarianism "Vegetarianism")" on [PETA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_for_the_Ethical_Treatment_of_Animals "People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals")'s yearly poll.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Veg-87) She was placed 68 on [_Maxim_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_(magazine) "Maxim (magazine)")'s 2005 "Hot 100" list,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-88) 11 in _Maxim_'s 2006 "Hot 100" list,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-89) and 46 in _Maxim_'s 2007 "Hot 100" list in which she was stated to have "single-handedly saved [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") from becoming the worst network ever".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-90) In 2006, _Maxim_ also placed Bell at the top of the "Fall TV's Criminally Sexy Investigators" List.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Veg-87) In 2008, she was ranked 59 on [AskMen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AskMen "AskMen")'s Top 99 Women of 2008 List.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-91) Reflecting on her admitted popularity with "geeks", Bell was voted the fourth-sexiest woman on TV by the staff at [_Wizard_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wizard_(magazine) "Wizard (magazine)").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-92)

Bell stated she never thought of herself as womanly because "I always play and look and act 10 years younger than I am." However, she said, "Something magical happened when I turned 25 — I looked in the mirror and was like, 'You might not get carded for an R-rated movie anymore.' Like I didn't have a little stick figure anymore."[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Complex-93) Bell has said that many of her characters are [tomboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomboy "Tomboy") because she was "not homely enough to play the [nerdy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerd "Nerd") girl and not nearly pretty enough to play the pretty girl".[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Complex-93)

What I like about nerdiness, [geekiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geek "Geek"), is it doesn't really matter what you're into—it just means you're not a follower."[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Complex-93) She has also said, "I love nerds. [Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic-Con_International "Comic-Con International") junkies are the tastemakers of tomorrow. Isn't that funny?
