### Relationships and family

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Relationships and family")]

[![Image 11: Photo of Dax Shepard and Kristen Bell, where Shepard is a head taller, Bell is wearing a multi-colored dress](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/Kristen_Bell%2C_Dax_Shepard_2012.jpg/250px-Kristen_Bell%2C_Dax_Shepard_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kristen_Bell,_Dax_Shepard_2012.jpg)

[Dax Shepard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dax_Shepard "Dax Shepard") and Bell at the 2012 [DoSomething](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoSomething "DoSomething") Awards

In 2007, Bell ended a five-year relationship with former fiancé Kevin Mann.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-102) She later told _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex\_(magazine) "Complex (magazine)")_ magazine that dating "makes me want to vomit. And not out of grossness—OK, a little bit out of grossness, but just nerves... I've always been a [serial monogamist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serial_monogamy "Serial monogamy")."[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Complex-93)

In late 2007, Bell began dating actor [Dax Shepard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dax_Shepard "Dax Shepard"), who is also from the [Detroit metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Detroit "Metro Detroit"). They announced their engagement in January 2010.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-103) They decided to delay marriage until the state of California passed legislation legalizing [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-104) They co-starred in the 2010 film _[When in Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When\_in\_Rome\_(2010\_film) "When in Rome (2010 film)")_, the 2012 film _[Hit and Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit\_and\_Run\_(2012\_film) "Hit and Run (2012 film)")_,[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-105) and the 2017 film _[CHiPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CHiPs\_(film) "CHiPs (film)")_. After section 3 of the [Defense of Marriage Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_of_Marriage_Act "Defense of Marriage Act") was ruled unconstitutional by the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Supreme_Court "U.S. Supreme Court") on June 26, 2013, Bell asked Shepard to marry her through Twitter,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Twitter-KristenProp-2013-106) which he accepted.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-DaxProp-2013-107) They were married at the [Beverly Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California") County Clerk's Office on October 16, 2013.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-108) They have two daughters, born in March 2013 and December 2014.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-110)

### Mental health

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Mental health")]

In May 2016, Bell said that she has received treatment for [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depression_(mood) "Depression (mood)") and [anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety_disorder "Anxiety disorder").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-111) She said, "It's important for me to be candid about this so people in a similar situation can realize that they are not worthless and that they do have something to offer."[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-112) In a March 2020 blog post, Bell wrote, "Don't be fooled by this game of perfection that humans play. Because Instagram and magazines and TV shows, they strive for a certain aesthetic, and everything looks so beautiful, and people seem like they don't have any problems, but everyone's human. Everyone has problems. Everyone feels yucky on the inside sometimes."[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-113)

In an interview with [Jimmy Kimmel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Kimmel "Jimmy Kimmel") in August 2018, Bell discussed why she wears scuba gloves while swimming. She stated that she fears the sensation of touching things with water-immersed, wrinkled fingers, otherwise known as "[prune fingers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prune_fingers "Prune fingers")". The gloves have allowed her to swim with her children without fearing touching them.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-114)

### Beliefs and interests

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Beliefs and interests")]

[![Image 12: Photo of Kristen Bell wearing a light hat fedora hat, resting her left hand on the neck of a light brown dog](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Kristen_Bell_2012.jpg/250px-Kristen_Bell_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kristen_Bell_2012.jpg)

Bell with the Dancing Merengue Dog at the [2012 Bonnaroo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Bonnaroo_Music_Festival "2012 Bonnaroo Music Festival")

At age 11, Bell became a [vegetarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetarianism "Vegetarianism").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Veg-87) In an interview with [PETA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PETA "PETA"), Bell discussed her pets, "I have always been an animal lover. I had a hard time disassociating the animals I cuddled with—dogs and cats, for example—from the animals on my plate, and I never really cared for the taste of meat. I always loved my [Brussels sprouts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_sprout "Brussels sprout")!"[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-autogenerated1-115) By 2012, Bell and Shepard had become [vegan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veganism "Veganism") after watching the documentary _[Forks Over Knives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forks\_Over\_Knives "Forks Over Knives")_.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-BellDax-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-117) However, during her first pregnancy she went back to eating dairy products and eggs.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-118) She started eating meat in 2022.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-119)

Bell has said that she is [non-religious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-religious "Non-religious") and identifies as a [humanist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanism "Humanism").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-people-maron-6) She and her husband Dax Shepard are pro-[vaccination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccination "Vaccination").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-121) Bell supported and campaigned for [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") during the [2008 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election "2008 United States presidential election"). Along with [Rashida Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashida_Jones "Rashida Jones"), she visited college campuses in [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") to discuss the candidates and encourage voter registration.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-124) Bell showed support for the [Writers Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America "Writers Guild of America") in the [writers' strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike"), appearing in the picket lines in December 2007, stating, "the writers are just looking for some fairness".[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-125)

In 2023, Bell revealed that she had taken up [Brazilian jiu-jitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_jiu-jitsu "Brazilian jiu-jitsu"). She was training under Cesalina Gracie in mother-daughter classes alongside her daughter.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-126)

### Charity work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Charity work")]

During her time in Michigan, Bell fostered animals from the [Michigan Humane Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_Humane_Society "Michigan Humane Society"), and she now supports the San Diego–based [Helen Woodward Animal Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Woodward_Animal_Center "Helen Woodward Animal Center"). Bell often attends fundraisers for the [American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_for_the_Prevention_of_Cruelty_to_Animals "American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals") and other non-profit organizations dedicated to protecting animals. She has had several dogs, including a [Welsh Corgi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_Corgi "Welsh Corgi")-[Chow Chow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chow_Chow "Chow Chow") mix named Lola, a Welsh Corgi-[Chihuahua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihuahua_(dog_breed) "Chihuahua (dog breed)") mix named Shakey and a black [Labrador Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador_Retriever "Labrador Retriever") named Sadie, who was 11-years-old when she was rescued from [Hurricane Katrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Katrina "Hurricane Katrina") and adopted by Bell in 2005.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Mars-10)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-127)

Bell and other _Veronica Mars_ cast members, including [Ryan Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Hansen "Ryan Hansen"), are involved with the charity [Invisible Children, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invisible_Children,_Inc. "Invisible Children, Inc.") The goal of the organization is to create awareness of the plight of [Northern Ugandans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Uganda "Northern Uganda") who are caught in the midst of a [civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_war "Civil war") between the government and [Joseph Kony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Kony "Joseph Kony")'s [Lord's Resistance Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Resistance_Army "Lord's Resistance Army").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-LoVe-128) In 2014, Bell launched a [Prizeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prizeo "Prizeo") campaign offering fans a chance to win a date with her in return for donating to Invisible Children, Inc.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-129) In 2018, Bell participated in a television advertisement for bone marrow donations, specifically the Gift of Life Marrow Registry. Her actions resulted in several matches that are documented on the Gift of Life website.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-130) Bell won a [2020 Webby Special Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Webby_Award "2020 Webby Award").[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-Kastrenakes-131)

In 2013, Kristen Bell, along with actors [Ryan Devlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Devlin "Ryan Devlin"), [Todd Grinnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Grinnell "Todd Grinnell"), and [Ravi Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravi_Patel_(actor) "Ravi Patel (actor)"), founded the granola bar company This Bar Saves Lives to help fight malnutrition. The business donates food aid in the form of nutrition packets to children in [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti"), [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan "South Sudan"), [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia"), and [Somalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia "Somalia"). Since its launch, the company has donated more than 10 million packets as of February 2019.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-132)

### Entrepreneurship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kristen_Bell&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Entrepreneurship")]

In 2019, Bell and her husband founded the company Hello Bello that markets plant-based baby care products said to be environmentally friendly and affordable.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-133) As of 2021, Hello Bello's estimated annual revenue was $26.1 million a year with 104 employees.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-134) In 2020, she partnered to start Happy Dance, a line of vegan CBD products such as eye cream and hand moisturizers. In 2023, Hello Bello filed for [Chapter 11 bankruptcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapter_11_bankruptcy "Chapter 11 bankruptcy"), blaming years of declining sales and the financial startup crisis. The company is set to be acquired by private equity firm Hildred Capital Management.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Bell#cite_note-135)

**Huntington Woods** is a city in [Oakland County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_County,_Michigan "Oakland County, Michigan") in the U.S. state of [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan "Michigan"). An inner-ring [suburb of Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Detroit "Metro Detroit") on the [Woodward Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodward_Corridor "Woodward Corridor"), Huntington Woods is located roughly 12 miles (19.3 km) northwest of [downtown Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Detroit "Downtown Detroit"). As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the city had a population of 6,388.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-4)

Huntington Woods is situated along the [Woodward Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodward_Corridor "Woodward Corridor") ([M-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M-1_(Michigan_highway) "M-1 (Michigan highway)")) and is bounded by Ten and Eleven Mile Roads to the north and south, and by Woodward and Coolidge Highway to the east and west. [Rackham Golf Course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rackham_Golf_Course "Rackham Golf Course") is located in the central southern side of the city. The western portion of the [Detroit Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Zoo "Detroit Zoo") is located within the city limits and is a contributor to its tax base.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 1.47 square miles (3.81 km 2), all land.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Gazetteer_files-5) Rackham Golf Course, owned by the city of Detroit, makes up 20% (0.3 square miles) of the total area of the city.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-6)

Huntington Woods is adjacent to the cities of [Pleasant Ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasant_Ridge,_Michigan "Pleasant Ridge, Michigan") to the southeast, [Oak Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Park,_Michigan "Oak Park, Michigan") to the south and west, [Royal Oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Oak,_Michigan "Royal Oak, Michigan") to the east, and [Berkley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkley,_Michigan "Berkley, Michigan") to the north.

Huntington Woods is bordered to the south by 10 Mile Road/[I-696](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_696 "Interstate 696"), to the west by Coolidge Highway, to the east by [Woodward Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodward_Avenue "Woodward Avenue") (M-1), and to the north by 11 Mile Road.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Huntington Woods had a population of 6,388. The median age was 43.1 years. 25.6% of residents were under the age of 18 and 19.0% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 94.2 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 91.1 males age 18 and over.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020DP-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020PL-10)

100.0% of residents lived in urban areas.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020DHC-11)

There were 2,375 households in Huntington Woods, of which 39.2% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 68.5% were married-couple households, 8.8% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 18.8% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 17.8% of all households were made up of individuals and 10.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020DP-9)

There were 2,428 housing units, of which 2.2% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.6% and the rental vacancy rate was 4.2%.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020DP-9)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-12) of 2010, there were 6,238 people, 2,354 households, and 1,784 families living in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 4,243.5 inhabitants per square mile (1,638.4/km 2). There were 2,429 housing units at an average density of 1,652.4 per square mile (638.0/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 96.0% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 1.0% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.2% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 1.3% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.5% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 1.1% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 1.6% of the population.

There were 2,354 households, of which 38.0% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 66.9% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 6.4% had a female householder with no husband present, 2.5% had a male householder with no wife present, and 24.2% were non-families. 19.8% of all households were made up of individuals, and 9.1% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.65 and the average family size was 3.08.

The median age in the city was 42 years. 27.4% of residents were under the age of 18; 3.8% were between the ages of 18 and 24; 23.6% were from 25 to 44; 31.6% were from 45 to 64; and 13.6% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the city was 49.2% male and 50.8% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-GR2-2) of 2000, there were 6,151 people, 2,381 households, and 1,802 families living in the city. The population density was 4,196.0 inhabitants per square mile (1,620.1/km 2). There were 2,416 housing units at an average density of 1,648.1 per square mile (636.3/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 96.96% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.68% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.05% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 1.41% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.26% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.63% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 0.88% of the population.

There were 2,381 households, out of which 37.6% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 67.2% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 7.0% had a female householder with no husband present, and 24.3% were non-families. 19.5% of all households were made up of individuals, and 7.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.58 and the average family size was 3.01.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 26.6% under the age of 18, 3.3% from 18 to 24, 27.8% from 25 to 44, 29.7% from 45 to 64, and 12.7% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 41 years. For every 100 females, there were 95.3 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 91.0 males.

The median income for a household in the city was $87,086, and the median income for a family was $97,055. Males had a median income of $73,750 versus $43,565 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $45,264. About 1.8% of families and 2.6% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 3.2% of those under age 18 and 2.3% of those age 65 or over.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Education")]

All residents live within [Berkley School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkley_School_District "Berkley School District") boundaries.

Many residents also attend local private schools, such as [University of Detroit Jesuit High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Detroit_Jesuit "University of Detroit Jesuit"), [Detroit Country Day School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Country_Day_School "Detroit Country Day School"), [Shrine Catholic High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_Catholic_High_School "Shrine Catholic High School"), [The Roeper School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roeper_School_(Michigan) "Roeper School (Michigan)"), [Farber Hebrew Day School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farber_Hebrew_Day_School "Farber Hebrew Day School"), [Hillel Day School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillel_Day_School "Hillel Day School"), [Cranbrook-Kingswood School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranbrook_Kingswood_School "Cranbrook Kingswood School"), [Brother Rice High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brother_Rice_High_School_(Michigan) "Brother Rice High School (Michigan)"), and [Mercy High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy_High_School_(Farmington_Hills,_Michigan) "Mercy High School (Farmington Hills, Michigan)").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

*   [Jef Mallett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jef_Mallett "Jef Mallett"), artist and writer of the syndicated comic strip [Frazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frazz "Frazz"), current resident
*   [Ellen Lipton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellen_Lipton "Ellen Lipton"), American politician and former Democratic member of the [Michigan State House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_House_of_Representatives "Michigan State House of Representatives")

**Huntington Woods** is a city in [Oakland County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_County,_Michigan "Oakland County, Michigan") in the U.S. state of [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan "Michigan"). An inner-ring [suburb of Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Detroit "Metro Detroit") on the [Woodward Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodward_Corridor "Woodward Corridor"), Huntington Woods is located roughly 12 miles (19.3 km) northwest of [downtown Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Detroit "Downtown Detroit"). As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the city had a population of 6,388.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-4)

Huntington Woods is situated along the [Woodward Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodward_Corridor "Woodward Corridor") ([M-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M-1_(Michigan_highway) "M-1 (Michigan highway)")) and is bounded by Ten and Eleven Mile Roads to the north and south, and by Woodward and Coolidge Highway to the east and west. [Rackham Golf Course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rackham_Golf_Course "Rackham Golf Course") is located in the central southern side of the city. The western portion of the [Detroit Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Zoo "Detroit Zoo") is located within the city limits and is a contributor to its tax base.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 1.47 square miles (3.81 km 2), all land.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Gazetteer_files-5) Rackham Golf Course, owned by the city of Detroit, makes up 20% (0.3 square miles) of the total area of the city.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-6)

Huntington Woods is adjacent to the cities of [Pleasant Ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasant_Ridge,_Michigan "Pleasant Ridge, Michigan") to the southeast, [Oak Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Park,_Michigan "Oak Park, Michigan") to the south and west, [Royal Oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Oak,_Michigan "Royal Oak, Michigan") to the east, and [Berkley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkley,_Michigan "Berkley, Michigan") to the north.

Huntington Woods is bordered to the south by 10 Mile Road/[I-696](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_696 "Interstate 696"), to the west by Coolidge Highway, to the east by [Woodward Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodward_Avenue "Woodward Avenue") (M-1), and to the north by 11 Mile Road.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Huntington Woods had a population of 6,388. The median age was 43.1 years. 25.6% of residents were under the age of 18 and 19.0% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 94.2 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 91.1 males age 18 and over.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020DP-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020PL-10)

100.0% of residents lived in urban areas.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020DHC-11)

There were 2,375 households in Huntington Woods, of which 39.2% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 68.5% were married-couple households, 8.8% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 18.8% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 17.8% of all households were made up of individuals and 10.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020DP-9)

There were 2,428 housing units, of which 2.2% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.6% and the rental vacancy rate was 4.2%.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-Census2020DP-9)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-12) of 2010, there were 6,238 people, 2,354 households, and 1,784 families living in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 4,243.5 inhabitants per square mile (1,638.4/km 2). There were 2,429 housing units at an average density of 1,652.4 per square mile (638.0/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 96.0% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 1.0% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.2% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 1.3% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.5% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 1.1% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 1.6% of the population.

There were 2,354 households, of which 38.0% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 66.9% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 6.4% had a female householder with no husband present, 2.5% had a male householder with no wife present, and 24.2% were non-families. 19.8% of all households were made up of individuals, and 9.1% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.65 and the average family size was 3.08.

The median age in the city was 42 years. 27.4% of residents were under the age of 18; 3.8% were between the ages of 18 and 24; 23.6% were from 25 to 44; 31.6% were from 45 to 64; and 13.6% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the city was 49.2% male and 50.8% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Woods,_Michigan#cite_note-GR2-2) of 2000, there were 6,151 people, 2,381 households, and 1,802 families living in the city. The population density was 4,196.0 inhabitants per square mile (1,620.1/km 2). There were 2,416 housing units at an average density of 1,648.1 per square mile (636.3/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 96.96% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.68% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.05% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 1.41% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.26% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.63% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 0.88% of the population.

There were 2,381 households, out of which 37.6% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 67.2% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 7.0% had a female householder with no husband present, and 24.3% were non-families. 19.5% of all households were made up of individuals, and 7.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.58 and the average family size was 3.01.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 26.6% under the age of 18, 3.3% from 18 to 24, 27.8% from 25 to 44, 29.7% from 45 to 64, and 12.7% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 41 years. For every 100 females, there were 95.3 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 91.0 males.

The median income for a household in the city was $87,086, and the median income for a family was $97,055. Males had a median income of $73,750 versus $43,565 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $45,264. About 1.8% of families and 2.6% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 3.2% of those under age 18 and 2.3% of those age 65 or over.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Huntington_Woods,_Michigan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Education")]

All residents live within [Berkley School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkley_School_District "Berkley School District") boundaries.

Many residents also attend local private schools, such as [University of Detroit Jesuit High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Detroit_Jesuit "University of Detroit Jesuit"), [Detroit Country Day School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Country_Day_School "Detroit Country Day School"), [Shrine Catholic High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_Catholic_High_School "Shrine Catholic High School"), [The Roeper School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roeper_School_(Michigan) "Roeper School (Michigan)"), [Farber Hebrew Day School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farber_Hebrew_Day_School "Farber Hebrew Day School"), [Hillel Day School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillel_Day_School "Hillel Day School"), [Cranbrook-Kingswood School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranbrook_Kingswood_School "Cranbrook Kingswood School"), [Brother Rice High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brother_Rice_High_School_(Michigan) "Brother Rice High School (Michigan)"), and [Mercy High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy_High_School_(Farmington_Hills,_Michigan) "Mercy High School (Farmington Hills, Michigan)").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

*   [Jef Mallett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jef_Mallett "Jef Mallett"), artist and writer of the syndicated comic strip [Frazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frazz "Frazz"), current resident
*   [Ellen Lipton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellen_Lipton "Ellen Lipton"), American politician and former Democratic member of the [Michigan State House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_House_of_Representatives "Michigan State House of Representatives")

#### ABOUT US

The City of Huntington Woods is in Southeastern Oakland County and is bounded by 11 Mile to the north, Woodward Avenue to the east, the I-696 Service Drive to the south and Coolidge Highway to the west. The City is located less than 15 miles northwest of downtown Detroit. Known as the “The City of Homes,” Huntington Woods is comprised of 2,364 homes with a population of 6,300 people. The City is home to a large section of the Detroit Zoo and Rackham Golf Course which is owned and operated by the City of Detroit.

#### ABOUT US

The City of Huntington Woods is in Southeastern Oakland County and is bounded by 11 Mile to the north, Woodward Avenue to the east, the I-696 Service Drive to the south and Coolidge Highway to the west. The City is located less than 15 miles northwest of downtown Detroit. Known as the “The City of Homes,” Huntington Woods is comprised of 2,364 homes with a population of 6,300 people. The City is home to a large section of the Detroit Zoo and Rackham Golf Course which is owned and operated by the City of Detroit.

# Huntington Woods MI Real Estate & Neighborhood Guide

Known as “The City of Homes,” Huntington Woods is made up entirely of charming, single-family residences.

## Welcome to Huntington Woods

_**Metro Detroit’s quaint “City of Homes,” minutes away from all the city has to offer**_

Conveniently located between Woodward Avenue and Interstate 696 lies the quiet and close-knit neighborhood of Huntington Woods. Just 12 miles north of downtown, Huntington Woods has become the perfect, quaint community for those working in inner Detroit who would like a central neighborhood, but may not want to be downtown full-time. Known as “The City of Homes,” Huntington Woods is made up entirely of charming, single-family residences.

Huntington Woods is an inner-ring suburb located within walking distance of downtown Royal Oak, and it is only a short drive from the downtowns of Ferndale and Birmingham. In addition to parks and recreational green space, Huntington Woods is also home to the [Rackham Golf Course](http://www.rackham.golf/) and the [Detroit Zoo](https://detroitzoo.org/). The Detroit Zoo is home to over 2,000 animals of 237 species, situated on 125 acres. As a result, the neighborhood is a unique enclave of tree-lined streets and manicured lawns only an arm’s length away from the conveniences and amenities of modern-day urban life.

### What to Love

*   Huntington Woods has affectionately been nicknamed the “City of Homes,” consisting entirely of single-family residences. 
*   A convenient location between Interstate 696 and Woodward Avenue, situated just 12 miles from downtown Detroit, has made this a popular spot for commuters. 
*   Tree-lined streets and lush, green, uniform front lawns give Huntington Woods a quaint and quiet vibe not found in many other parts of the city. 

### Local Lifestyle

Life in Huntington Woods is largely peaceful. Residents tend to spend free time close to home at one of their many local parks. Greenspaces, playgrounds, sports courts, and other fields offer ample options for getting some fresh air. Another option is the [Rackham Golf Course](http://www.rackham.golf/), owned by the city of Detroit. Rackham has consistently been named one of the best municipal golf courses in Michigan. With a central location and easy access to freeways, short trips to neighboring communities are quick and easy.

### Dining, Entertainment, & Shopping

Huntington Woods specifically is a community made up entirely of single-family homes. However, their close proximity to many of Detroit's major thoroughfares makes it easy to get out and grab a quick bite or sip without venturing too far from home. The neighborhoods surrounding Huntington Woods pay tribute to the storied past of the Motor City, with locally-owned and operated businesses situated in historic settings.

While working from home has become more common in recent years, sometimes a day out of the house is necessary. This is where The Office Coffee Shop comes into play. The Office truly is the best of both worlds. One half is open to the public with a full menu of coffee, pastries, and other snacks. The other half consists of a co-working environment with private offices for rent, space available for events, and professional services specially tailored to start-ups and entrepreneurs.

More relaxed mornings off-the-clock can be spent at [O.W.L.](https://owlwoodward.com/) Specializing in breakfast, brunch, and late-night snacks, they are open from early till late seven days a week. Some of their early-morning and late-night features include fried chicken, tacos, decked-out avocado toast, and classic breakfast sandwiches, all crafted to hit the spot.

If a night out on the town is needed, [Vinsetta Garage](https://www.vinsettagarage.com/) is a Detroit favorite, located in the oldest garage east of the Mississippi River. The completely transformed space is reminiscent of past times - featuring an extensive lineup of unique burgers, one of the best macaroni and cheese dishes the Detroit area has to offer, and foods originally craved by the founding workers of the Motor City.

### Things To Do

Although Huntington Woods is entirely residential, major entertainment is located just a few streets away. Two popular attractions include the [Rackham Golf Course](http://www.rackham.golf/), consistently rated as one of the best municipal golf courses in the area, and the [Detroit Zoo](https://detroitzoo.org/). Huntington Woods residents also benefit from living in close proximity to the many local parks. The most centrally located of these is Huntington Woods Park, consisting of playgrounds, endless green spaces, and a Little Free Library.

### Schools

Another reason Huntington Woods is so well-liked is the presence of highly-rated schools within the area. One of the best-known educational opportunities is:

*   [Berkley Schools](https://www.berkleyschools.org/), kindergarten-12th grade; the CASA program (Center for Advanced Studies and the Arts) is available, providing students with advanced placement courses, an exceptional visual arts curriculum, and an advanced dance program

# Huntington Woods MI Real Estate & Neighborhood Guide

Known as “The City of Homes,” Huntington Woods is made up entirely of charming, single-family residences.

## Welcome to Huntington Woods

_**Metro Detroit’s quaint “City of Homes,” minutes away from all the city has to offer**_

Conveniently located between Woodward Avenue and Interstate 696 lies the quiet and close-knit neighborhood of Huntington Woods. Just 12 miles north of downtown, Huntington Woods has become the perfect, quaint community for those working in inner Detroit who would like a central neighborhood, but may not want to be downtown full-time. Known as “The City of Homes,” Huntington Woods is made up entirely of charming, single-family residences.

Huntington Woods is an inner-ring suburb located within walking distance of downtown Royal Oak, and it is only a short drive from the downtowns of Ferndale and Birmingham. In addition to parks and recreational green space, Huntington Woods is also home to the [Rackham Golf Course](http://www.rackham.golf/) and the [Detroit Zoo](https://detroitzoo.org/). The Detroit Zoo is home to over 2,000 animals of 237 species, situated on 125 acres. As a result, the neighborhood is a unique enclave of tree-lined streets and manicured lawns only an arm’s length away from the conveniences and amenities of modern-day urban life.

### What to Love

*   Huntington Woods has affectionately been nicknamed the “City of Homes,” consisting entirely of single-family residences. 
*   A convenient location between Interstate 696 and Woodward Avenue, situated just 12 miles from downtown Detroit, has made this a popular spot for commuters. 
*   Tree-lined streets and lush, green, uniform front lawns give Huntington Woods a quaint and quiet vibe not found in many other parts of the city. 

### Local Lifestyle

Life in Huntington Woods is largely peaceful. Residents tend to spend free time close to home at one of their many local parks. Greenspaces, playgrounds, sports courts, and other fields offer ample options for getting some fresh air. Another option is the [Rackham Golf Course](http://www.rackham.golf/), owned by the city of Detroit. Rackham has consistently been named one of the best municipal golf courses in Michigan. With a central location and easy access to freeways, short trips to neighboring communities are quick and easy.

### Dining, Entertainment, & Shopping

Huntington Woods specifically is a community made up entirely of single-family homes. However, their close proximity to many of Detroit's major thoroughfares makes it easy to get out and grab a quick bite or sip without venturing too far from home. The neighborhoods surrounding Huntington Woods pay tribute to the storied past of the Motor City, with locally-owned and operated businesses situated in historic settings.

While working from home has become more common in recent years, sometimes a day out of the house is necessary. This is where The Office Coffee Shop comes into play. The Office truly is the best of both worlds. One half is open to the public with a full menu of coffee, pastries, and other snacks. The other half consists of a co-working environment with private offices for rent, space available for events, and professional services specially tailored to start-ups and entrepreneurs.

More relaxed mornings off-the-clock can be spent at [O.W.L.](https://owlwoodward.com/) Specializing in breakfast, brunch, and late-night snacks, they are open from early till late seven days a week. Some of their early-morning and late-night features include fried chicken, tacos, decked-out avocado toast, and classic breakfast sandwiches, all crafted to hit the spot.

If a night out on the town is needed, [Vinsetta Garage](https://www.vinsettagarage.com/) is a Detroit favorite, located in the oldest garage east of the Mississippi River. The completely transformed space is reminiscent of past times - featuring an extensive lineup of unique burgers, one of the best macaroni and cheese dishes the Detroit area has to offer, and foods originally craved by the founding workers of the Motor City.

### Things To Do

Although Huntington Woods is entirely residential, major entertainment is located just a few streets away. Two popular attractions include the [Rackham Golf Course](http://www.rackham.golf/), consistently rated as one of the best municipal golf courses in the area, and the [Detroit Zoo](https://detroitzoo.org/). Huntington Woods residents also benefit from living in close proximity to the many local parks. The most centrally located of these is Huntington Woods Park, consisting of playgrounds, endless green spaces, and a Little Free Library.

### Schools

Another reason Huntington Woods is so well-liked is the presence of highly-rated schools within the area. One of the best-known educational opportunities is:

*   [Berkley Schools](https://www.berkleyschools.org/), kindergarten-12th grade; the CASA program (Center for Advanced Studies and the Arts) is available, providing students with advanced placement courses, an exceptional visual arts curriculum, and an advanced dance program
